gene.name: ATP binding cassette subfamily D member 1
gene.function: ATP-dependent transporter of the ATP-binding cassette (ABC) family involved in the transport of very long chain fatty acid (VLCFA)- CoA from the cytosol to the peroxisome lumen. Coupled to the ATP- dependent transporter activity also has a fatty acyl-CoA thioesterase activity (ACOT) and hydrolyzes VLCFA-CoA into VLCFA prior their ATP- dependent transport into peroxisomes, the ACOT activity is essential during this transport process. Thus, plays a role in regulation of VLCFAs and energy metabolism namely, in the degradation and biosynthesis of fatty acids by beta-oxidation, mitochondrial function and microsomal fatty acid elongation. Involved in several processes; namely, controls the active myelination phase by negatively regulating the microsomal fatty acid elongation activity and may also play a role in axon and myelin maintenance. Also controls the cellular response to oxidative stress by regulating mitochondrial functions such as mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation and depolarization. And finally controls the inflammatory response by positively regulating peroxisomal beta-oxidation of VLCFAs (By similarity).

gene.name: arylsulfatase A
gene.function: Lysosomal enzyme that catalyzes the hydrolysis of cerebroside-3-sulfate (N-acyl-1-beta-D-(3-O-sulfo)-galactosyl-sphing-4- enine) into cerebroside and sulfate, a reaction that requires the activator protein saposin B. Also involved in the catabolism of other sulfoglycosphingolipids such as SB1a and SM3 (beta-D-3-sulfogalactosyl- (1->4)-beta-D-glucosyl-(1<->1')-N-acylsphing-4-enine) (By similarity).

gene.name: N-acylsphingosine amidohydrolase 1
gene.function: Lysosomal ceramidase that hydrolyzes sphingolipid ceramides into sphingosine and free fatty acids at acidic pH. Ceramides, sphingosine, and its phosphorylated form sphingosine-1-phosphate are bioactive lipids that mediate cellular signaling pathways regulating several biological processes including cell proliferation, apoptosis and differentiation. Has a higher catalytic efficiency towards C12- ceramides versus other ceramides. Also catalyzes the reverse reaction allowing the synthesis of ceramides from fatty acids and sphingosine. For the reverse synthetic reaction, the natural sphingosine D-erythro isomer is more efficiently utilized as a substrate compared to D- erythro-dihydrosphingosine and D-erythro-phytosphingosine, while the fatty acids with chain lengths of 12 or 14 carbons are the most efficiently used. Also has an N-acylethanolamine hydrolase activity. By regulating the levels of ceramides, sphingosine and sphingosine-1-phosphate in the epidermis, mediates the calcium-induced differentiation of epidermal keratinocytes. Also indirectly regulates tumor necrosis factor/TNF- induced apoptosis (By similarity). By regulating the intracellular balance between ceramides and sphingosine, in adrenocortical cells, probably also acts as a regulator of steroidogenesis.

gene.name: activating transcription factor 3
gene.function: This protein binds the cAMP response element (CRE) (consensus: 5'-GTGACGT[AC][AG]-3'), a sequence present in many viral and cellular promoters. Represses transcription from promoters with ATF sites. It may repress transcription by stabilizing the binding of inhibitory cofactors at the promoter. .

gene.name: ATPase cation transporting 13A2
gene.function: ATPase which acts as a lysosomal polyamine exporter with high affinity for spermine. Also stimulates cellular uptake of polyamines and protects against polyamine toxicity. Plays a role in intracellular cation homeostasis and the maintenance of neuronal integrity. Contributes to cellular zinc homeostasis. Confers cellular protection against Mn(2+) and Zn(2+) toxicity and mitochondrial stress. Required for proper lysosomal and mitochondrial maintenance. Regulates the autophagy-lysosome pathway through the control of SYT11 expression at both transcriptional and post-translational levels. Facilitates recruitment of deacetylase HDAC6 to lysosomes to deacetylate CTTN, leading to actin polymerization, promotion of autophagosome-lysosome fusion and completion of autophagy. Promotes secretion of exosomes as well as secretion of SCNA via exosomes. Plays a role in lipid homeostasis.

gene.name: ATPase H+ transporting V1 subunit G1
gene.function: Subunit of the V1 complex of vacuolar(H+)-ATPase (V-ATPase), a multisubunit enzyme composed of a peripheral complex (V1) that hydrolyzes ATP and a membrane integral complex (V0) that translocates protons. V-ATPase is responsible for acidifying and maintaining the pH of intracellular compartments and in some cell types, is targeted to the plasma membrane, where it promotes acidification of the extracellular environment. The V-ATPase complex also acts as an activator for mTORC1 on lysosomal membrane by promoting the guanine nucleotide exchange factor (GEF) of the Ragulator complex, thereby enabling mTORC1 recruitment. In aerobic conditions, involved in intracellular iron homeostasis, thus triggering the activity of Fe(2+) prolyl hydroxylase (PHD) enzymes, and leading to HIF1A hydroxylation and subsequent proteasomal degradation.

gene.name: CF transmembrane conductance regulator
gene.function: Epithelial ion channel that plays an important role in the regulation of epithelial ion and water transport and fluid homeostasis. Mediates the transport of chloride ions across the cell membrane. Possesses an intrinsic ATPase activity and utilizes ATP to gate its channel; the passive flow of anions through the channel is gated by cycles of ATP binding and hydrolysis by the ATP-binding domains. The ion channel is also permeable to HCO(3)(-); selectivity depends on the extracellular chloride concentration. In vitro, mediates ATP-dependent glutathione flux. Exerts its function also by modulating the activity of other ion channels and transporters. Plays an important role in airway fluid homeostasis. Contributes to the regulation of the pH and the ion content of the airway surface fluid layer and thereby plays an important role in defense against pathogens. Modulates the activity of the epithelial sodium channel (ENaC) complex, in part by regulating the cell surface expression of the ENaC complex. Inhibits the activity of the ENaC channel containing subunits SCNN1A, SCNN1B and SCNN1G. Inhibits the activity of the ENaC channel containing subunits SCNN1D, SCNN1B and SCNN1G, but not of the ENaC channel containing subunits SCNN1A, SCNN1B and SCNN1G. May regulate bicarbonate secretion and salvage in epithelial cells by regulating the transporter SLC4A7. Can inhibit the chloride channel activity of ANO1. Plays a role in the chloride and bicarbonate homeostasis during sperm epididymal maturation and capacitation.

gene.name: galactosylceramidase
gene.function: Hydrolyzes the galactose ester bonds of glycolipids such as galactosylceramide and galactosylsphingosine. Enzyme with very low activity responsible for the lysosomal catabolism of galactosylceramide, a major lipid in myelin, kidney and epithelial cells of small intestine and colon.

gene.name: glucosylceramidase beta 1
gene.function: Glucosylceramidase that catalyzes, within the lysosomal compartment, the hydrolysis of glucosylceramides/GlcCers (such as beta- D-glucosyl-(1<->1')-N-acylsphing-4-enine) into free ceramides (such as N-acylsphing-4-enine) and glucose. Plays a central role in the degradation of complex lipids and the turnover of cellular membranes. Through the production of ceramides, participates in the PKC-activated salvage pathway of ceramide formation. Catalyzes the glucosylation of cholesterol, through a transglucosylation reaction where glucose is transferred from GlcCer to cholesterol. GlcCer containing mono-unsaturated fatty acids (such as beta-D- glucosyl-N-(9Z-octadecenoyl)-sphing-4-enine) are preferred as glucose donors for cholesterol glucosylation when compared with GlcCer containing same chain length of saturated fatty acids (such as beta-D- glucosyl-N-octadecanoyl-sphing-4-enine). Under specific conditions, may alternatively catalyze the reverse reaction, transferring glucose from cholesteryl 3-beta-D-glucoside to ceramide (Probable). Can also hydrolyze cholesteryl 3-beta-D- glucoside producing glucose and cholesterol. Catalyzes the hydrolysis of galactosylceramides/GalCers (such as beta-D-galactosyl-(1<->1')-N- acylsphing-4-enine), as well as the transfer of galactose between GalCers and cholesterol in vitro, but with lower activity than with GlcCers. Contrary to GlcCer and GalCer, xylosylceramide/XylCer (such as beta-D-xyosyl-(1<->1')-N-acylsphing-4- enine) is not a good substrate for hydrolysis, however it is a good xylose donor for transxylosylation activity to form cholesteryl 3-beta- D-xyloside. Can also metabolize plant glycosyl phytosterols such as glucosylstigmasterol.

gene.name: insulin like growth factor 2 receptor
gene.function: Mediates the transport of phosphorylated lysosomal enzymes from the Golgi complex and the cell surface to lysosomes. Lysosomal enzymes bearing phosphomannosyl residues bind specifically to mannose-6-phosphate receptors in the Golgi apparatus and the resulting receptor-ligand complex is transported to an acidic prelysosomal compartment where the low pH mediates the dissociation of the complex. The receptor is then recycled back to the Golgi for another round of trafficking through its binding to the retromer. This receptor also binds IGF2. Acts as a positive regulator of T-cell coactivation by binding DPP4.

gene.name: interleukin 2 receptor subunit gamma
gene.function: Common subunit for the receptors for a variety of interleukins. Probably in association with IL15RA, involved in the stimulation of neutrophil phagocytosis by IL15. .

gene.name: interleukin 6
gene.function: Cytokine with a wide variety of biological functions in immunity, tissue regeneration, and metabolism. Binds to IL6R, then the complex associates to the signaling subunit IL6ST/gp130 to trigger the intracellular IL6-signaling pathway (Probable). The interaction with the membrane-bound IL6R and IL6ST stimulates 'classic signaling', whereas the binding of IL6 and soluble IL6R to IL6ST stimulates 'trans- signaling'. Alternatively, 'cluster signaling' occurs when membrane- bound IL6:IL6R complexes on transmitter cells activate IL6ST receptors on neighboring receiver cells (Probable). .

gene.name: myelin basic protein
gene.function: The classic group of MBP isoforms (isoform 4-isoform 14) are with PLP the most abundant protein components of the myelin membrane in the CNS. They have a role in both its formation and stabilization. The smaller isoforms might have an important role in remyelination of denuded axons in multiple sclerosis. The non-classic group of MBP isoforms (isoform 1-isoform 3/Golli-MBPs) may preferentially have a role in the early developing brain long before myelination, maybe as components of transcriptional complexes, and may also be involved in signaling pathways in T-cells and neural cells. Differential splicing events combined with optional post-translational modifications give a wide spectrum of isomers, with each of them potentially having a specialized function. Induces T-cell proliferation. .

gene.name: mucolipin TRP cation channel 1
gene.function: Nonselective cation channel probably playing a role in the regulation of membrane trafficking events and of metal homeostasis. Acts as a Ca(2+)-permeable cation channel with inwardly rectifying activity. Proposed to play a major role in Ca(2+) release from late endosome and lysosome vesicles to the cytoplasm, which is important for many lysosome-dependent cellular events, including the fusion and trafficking of these organelles, exocytosis and autophagy. Required for efficient uptake of large particles in macrophages in which Ca(2+) release from the lysosomes triggers lysosomal exocytosis. May also play a role in phagosome-lysosome fusion (By similarity). Involved in lactosylceramide trafficking indicative for a role in the regulation of late endocytic membrane fusion/fission events. By mediating lysosomal Ca(2+) release is involved in regulation of mTORC1 signaling and in mTOR/TFEB-dependent lysosomal adaptation to environmental cues such as nutrient levels. Seems to act as lysosomal active oxygen species (ROS) sensor involved in ROS-induced TFEB activation and autophagy. Also functions as a Fe(2+) permeable channel in late endosomes and lysosomes. Also permeable to Mg(2+), Na(+), K(+) and Cs(+) (By similarity). Proposed to play a role in zinc homeostasis probably implicating its association with TMEM163 In adaptive immunity, TRPML2 and TRPML1 may play redundant roles in the function of the specialized lysosomes of B cells (By similarity).

gene.name: oligodendrocyte transcription factor 2
gene.function: Required for oligodendrocyte and motor neuron specification in the spinal cord, as well as for the development of somatic motor neurons in the hindbrain. Works in coordination with ZNF488 to promote oligodendrocyte differentiation. Orchestrates progenitor cell fates during cortical gliogenesis and gliomagenesis. In cooperation with OLIG2, activates oligodendrocyte precursor cells (OPCs) formation while repressing the generation of olfactory bulb interneuron intermediate progenitors (OBIN) generation through transcriptional regulation of GSX2. Mechanistically, binds and silences multiple conserved enhancer elements of GSX2. Cooperates with OLIG1 to establish the pMN domain of the embryonic neural tube. Antagonist of V2 interneuron and of NKX2-2- induced V3 interneuron development. .

gene.name: PPARG coactivator 1 alpha
gene.function: Transcriptional coactivator for steroid receptors and nuclear receptors. Greatly increases the transcriptional activity of PPARG and thyroid hormone receptor on the uncoupling protein promoter. Can regulate key mitochondrial genes that contribute to the program of adaptive thermogenesis. Plays an essential role in metabolic reprogramming in response to dietary availability through coordination of the expression of a wide array of genes involved in glucose and fatty acid metabolism. Acts as a key regulator of gluconeogenesis: stimulates hepatic gluconeogenesis by increasing the expression of gluconeogenic enzymes, and acting together with FOXO1 to promote the fasting gluconeogenic program. Induces the expression of PERM1 in the skeletal muscle in an ESRRA- dependent manner. Also involved in the integration of the circadian rhythms and energy metabolism (By similarity). Required for oscillatory expression of clock genes, such as BMAL1 and NR1D1, through the coactivation of RORA and RORC, and metabolic genes, such as PDK4 and PEPCK (By similarity).

gene.name: palmitoyl-protein thioesterase 1
gene.function: Has thioesterase activity against fatty acid thioesters with 14 -18 carbons, including palmitoyl-CoA, S-palmitoyl-N- acetylcysteamine, and palmitoylated proteins. In contrast to PPT2, PPT1 can hydrolyze palmitoylated proteins and palmitoylcysteine.

gene.name: prosaposin
gene.function: Saposins are specific low-molecular mass non-enzymatic glycoproteins that act as activator proteins for lysosomal sphingolipid-degrading enzymes, facilitating the hydrolysis of sphingolipids by extracting lipid substrates from membranes and presenting them to their respective enzymes. They are derived from a common precursor protein, prosaposin, which is proteolytically cleaved to yield four homologous proteins (saposin A, B, C, and D), each with distinct but partially overlapping lipid and enzyme specificities. .

gene.name: synuclein alpha
gene.function: Neuronal protein that plays several roles in synaptic activity such as regulation of synaptic vesicle trafficking and subsequent neurotransmitter release. Participates as a monomer in synaptic vesicle exocytosis by enhancing vesicle priming, fusion and dilation of exocytotic fusion pores. Mechanistically, acts by increasing local Ca(2+) release from microdomains which is essential for the enhancement of ATP-induced exocytosis. Also acts as a molecular chaperone in its multimeric membrane-bound state, assisting in the folding of synaptic fusion components called SNAREs (Soluble NSF Attachment Protein REceptors) at presynaptic plasma membrane in conjunction with cysteine string protein-alpha/DNAJC5. This chaperone activity is important to sustain normal SNARE-complex assembly during aging. Also plays a role in the regulation of the dopamine neurotransmission by associating with the dopamine transporter (DAT1) and thereby modulating its activity.

gene.name: superoxide dismutase 1
gene.function: Destroys radicals which are normally produced within the cells and which are toxic to biological systems. Catalyzes the oxidation of hydrogen sulfide (H2S) to sulfate, playing an important role in detoxifying H2S and limiting the accumulation of reactive sulfur species (RSS) such as persulfides and polysulfides.

gene.name: transcription factor A, mitochondrial
gene.function: Binds to the mitochondrial light strand promoter and functions in mitochondrial transcription regulation. Component of the mitochondrial transcription initiation complex, composed at least of TFB2M, TFAM and POLRMT that is required for basal transcription of mitochondrial DNA. In this complex, TFAM recruits POLRMT to a specific promoter whereas TFB2M induces structural changes in POLRMT to enable promoter opening and trapping of the DNA non-template strand. Required for accurate and efficient promoter recognition by the mitochondrial RNA polymerase. Promotes transcription initiation from the HSP1 and the light strand promoter by binding immediately upstream of transcriptional start sites. Is able to unwind DNA. Bends the mitochondrial light strand promoter DNA into a U-turn shape via its HMG boxes. Required for maintenance of normal levels of mitochondrial DNA. May play a role in organizing and compacting mitochondrial DNA.

gene.name: toll like receptor 2
gene.function: Cooperates with LY96 to mediate the innate immune response to bacterial lipoproteins and other microbial cell wall components. Cooperates with TLR1 or TLR6 to mediate the innate immune response to bacterial lipoproteins or lipopeptides. Acts via MYD88 and TRAF6, leading to NF-kappa-B activation, cytokine secretion and the inflammatory response. May also activate immune cells and promote apoptosis in response to the lipid moiety of lipoproteins. Recognizes mycoplasmal macrophage-activating lipopeptide-2kD (MALP-2), soluble tuberculosis factor (STF), phenol-soluble modulin (PSM) and B.burgdorferi outer surface protein A lipoprotein (OspA-L) cooperatively with TLR6. Stimulation of monocytes in vitro with M.tuberculosis PstS1 induces p38 MAPK and ERK1/2 activation primarily via this receptor, but also partially via TLR4. MAPK activation in response to bacterial peptidoglycan also occurs via this receptor. Acts as a receptor for M.tuberculosis lipoproteins LprA, LprG, LpqH and PstS1, some lipoproteins are dependent on other coreceptors (TLR1, CD14 and/or CD36); the lipoproteins act as agonists to modulate antigen presenting cell functions in response to the pathogen. M.tuberculosis HSP70 (dnaK) but not HSP65 (groEL-2) acts via this protein to stimulate NF-kappa-B expression. Recognizes M.tuberculosis major T-antigen EsxA (ESAT-6) which inhibits downstream MYD88-dependent signaling (shown in mouse) (By similarity). Forms activation clusters composed of several receptors depending on the ligand, these clusters trigger signaling from the cell surface and subsequently are targeted to the Golgi in a lipid-raft dependent pathway. Forms the cluster TLR2:TLR6:CD14:CD36 in response to diacylated lipopeptides and TLR2:TLR1:CD14 in response to triacylated lipopeptides. Required for normal uptake of M.tuberculosis, a process that is inhibited by M.tuberculosis LppM (By similarity).

gene.name: transmembrane protein 106B
gene.function: In neurons, involved in the transport of late endosomes/lysosomes. May be involved in dendrite morphogenesis and maintenance by regulating lysosomal trafficking. May act as a molecular brake for retrograde transport of late endosomes/lysosomes, possibly via its interaction with MAP6 (By similarity). In motoneurons, may mediate the axonal transport of lysosomes and axonal sorting at the initial segment (By similarity). It remains unclear whether TMEM106B affects the transport of moving lysosomes in the anterograde or retrograde direction in neurites and whether it is important in the sorting of lysosomes in axons or in dendrites (By similarity). In neurons, may also play a role in the regulation of lysosomal size and responsiveness to stress. Required for proper lysosomal acidification (By similarity).

gene.name: transient receptor potential cation channel subfamily A member 1
gene.function: Ligand-activated Ca(2+)-permeable, nonselective cation channel involved in pain detection and possibly also in cold perception, oxygen concentration perception, cough, itch, and inner ear function. Has a relatively high Ca(2+) selectivity, with a preference for divalent over monovalent cations (Ca(2+) > Ba(2+) > Mg(2+) > NH4(+) > Li(+) > K(+)), the influx of cation into the cytoplasm leads to membrane depolarization. Has a central role in the pain response to endogenous inflammatory mediators, such as bradykinin and to a diverse array of irritants. Activated by a large variety of structurally unrelated electrophilic and non-electrophilic chemical compounds, such as allylthiocyanate (AITC) from mustard oil or wasabi, cinnamaldehyde, diallyl disulfide (DADS) from garlic, and acrolein, an environmental irritant. Electrophilic ligands activate TRPA1 by interacting with critical N-terminal Cys residues in a covalent manner. Non-electrophile agonists bind at distinct sites in the transmembrane domain to promote channel activation. Also acts as an ionotropic cannabinoid receptor by being activated by delta(9)-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC), the psychoactive component of marijuana. May be a component for the mechanosensitive transduction channel of hair cells in inner ear, thereby participating in the perception of sounds (By similarity).

gene.name: UDP-glucose ceramide glucosyltransferase
gene.function: Participates in the initial step of the glucosylceramide- based glycosphingolipid/GSL synthetic pathway at the cytosolic surface of the Golgi. Catalyzes the transfer of glucose from UDP-glucose to ceramide to produce glucosylceramide/GlcCer (such as beta-D-glucosyl-(1<->1')-N-acylsphing- 4-enine). GlcCer is the core component of glycosphingolipids/GSLs, amphipathic molecules consisting of a ceramide lipid moiety embedded in the outer leaflet of the membrane, linked to one of hundreds of different externally oriented oligosaccharide structures. Glycosphingolipids are essential components of membrane microdomains that mediate membrane trafficking and signal transduction, implicated in many fundamental cellular processes, including growth, differentiation, migration, morphogenesis, cell-to-cell and cell-to-matrix interactions (By similarity). They are required for instance in the proper development and functioning of the nervous system (By similarity). As an example of their role in signal transduction, they regulate the leptin receptor/LEPR in the leptin-mediated signaling pathway (By similarity). They also play an important role in the establishment of the skin barrier regulating keratinocyte differentiation and the proper assembly of the cornified envelope (By similarity). The biosynthesis of GSLs is also required for the proper intestinal endocytic uptake of nutritional lipids (By similarity). Catalyzes the synthesis of xylosylceramide/XylCer (such as beta-D-xylosyl-(1<->1')-N-acylsphing-4- enine) using UDP-Xyl as xylose donor.

gene.name: UDP glycosyltransferase 8
gene.function: Catalyzes the transfer of galactose to ceramide, a key enzymatic step in the biosynthesis of galactocerebrosides, which are abundant sphingolipids of the myelin membrane of the central nervous system and peripheral nervous system. Galactosylates both hydroxy- and non-hydroxy fatty acid-containing ceramides and diglycerides (By similarity).

gene.name: voltage dependent anion channel 1
gene.function: Non-selective voltage-gated ion channel that mediates the transport of anions and cations through the mitochondrion outer membrane and plasma membrane. The channel at the outer mitochondrial membrane allows diffusion of small hydrophilic molecules; in the plasma membrane it is involved in cell volume regulation and apoptosis. It adopts an open conformation at low or zero membrane potential and a closed conformation at potentials above 30-40 mV. The open state has a weak anion selectivity whereas the closed state is cation-selective. Binds various signaling molecules, including the sphingolipid ceramide, the phospholipid phosphatidylcholine, and the sterols cholesterol and oxysterol. In depolarized mitochondria, acts downstream of PRKN and PINK1 to promote mitophagy or prevent apoptosis; polyubiquitination by PRKN promotes mitophagy, while monoubiquitination by PRKN decreases mitochondrial calcium influx which ultimately inhibits apoptosis. May participate in the formation of the permeability transition pore complex (PTPC) responsible for the release of mitochondrial products that triggers apoptosis. May mediate ATP export from cells. Part of a complex composed of HSPA9, ITPR1 and VDAC1 that regulates mitochondrial calcium-dependent apoptosis by facilitating calcium transport from the ER lumen to the mitochondria intermembrane space thus providing calcium for the downstream calcium channel MCU that directly releases it into mitochondria matrix (By similarity). Mediates cytochrome c efflux.

gene.name: VPS33A core subunit of CORVET and HOPS complexes
gene.function: Plays a role in vesicle-mediated protein trafficking to lysosomal compartments including the endocytic membrane transport and autophagic pathways. Believed to act as a core component of the putative HOPS and CORVET endosomal tethering complexes which are proposed to be involved in the Rab5-to-Rab7 endosome conversion probably implicating MON1A/B, and via binding SNAREs and SNARE complexes to mediate tethering and docking events during SNARE-mediated membrane fusion. The HOPS complex is proposed to be recruited to Rab7 on the late endosomal membrane and to regulate late endocytic, phagocytic and autophagic traffic towards lysosomes. The CORVET complex is proposed to function as a Rab5 effector to mediate early endosome fusion probably in specific endosome subpopulations. Required for fusion of endosomes and autophagosomes with lysosomes; the function is dependent on its association with VPS16 but not VIPAS39. The function in autophagosome-lysosome fusion implicates STX17 but not UVRAG.

phenotype.definition: Any anomaly in the process by which myelin sheaths are formed and maintained around neurons.

Blindness is the condition of lacking visual perception defined as a profound reduction in visual perception. On the 6m visual acuity scale, blindness is defined as less than 3/60. On the 20ft visual acuity scale, blindness is defined as less than 20/400. On the decimal visual acuity scale, blindness is defined as less than 0.05. Blindness is typically characterized by a visual field of no greater than 10 degrees in radius around central fixation.
A loss of myelin from nerve fibers in the central nervous system.
Abnormal cognition is characterized by deficits in thinking, reasoning, or remembering.
Loss of developmental skills, as manifested by loss of developmental milestones.
An impairment of memory as manifested by a reduced ability to remember things such as dates and names, and increased forgetfulness.
Loss of previously present motor (i.e., movement) abilities.
Progressive loss of neural cells and tissue.

Characteristic neurologic anomaly resulting from degeneration of dopamine-generating cells in the substantia nigra, a region of the midbrain, characterized clinically by shaking, rigidity, slowness of movement and difficulty with walking and gait.
A loss of myelin from the internode regions along myelinated nerve fibers of the peripheral nervous system.

Peripheral neuropathy is a general term for any disorder of the peripheral nervous system. The main clinical features used to classify peripheral neuropathy are distribution, type (mainly demyelinating versus mainly axonal), duration, and course.
Spasticity that increases in degree with time.
Bleeding located within the retina. Retinal hemorrhages range from the smallest dot and blot hemorrhage to massive sub-hyaloid hemorrhage.
A motor disorder characterized by a velocity-dependent increase in tonic stretch reflexes with increased muscle tone, exaggerated (hyperexcitable) tendon reflexes.
phenotype.lay: Involuntary muscle stiffness, contraction, or spasm

phenotype.definition: An unintentional, oscillating to-and-fro muscle movement about a joint axis.

Visual impairment (or vision impairment) is vision loss (of a person) to such a degree as to qualify as an additional support need through a significant limitation of visual capability resulting from either disease, trauma, or congenital or degenerative conditions that cannot be corrected by conventional means, such as refractive correction, medication, or surgery.

literature.query: (TITLE_ABS:"ultra-low-intensity ultrasound stimulation") AND (TITLE_ABS:"Krabbe disease" OR TITLE_ABS:"diffuse globoid body sclerosis" OR TITLE_ABS:"galactocerebrosidase deficiency" OR TITLE_ABS:"galactosylceramidase deficiency" OR TITLE_ABS:"galactosylceramide lipidosis" OR TITLE_ABS:"GALC deficiency")

gaps.rationale: Ultra-low-intensity ultrasound has experimental evidence for reducing α-synuclein aggregation, but this pathway is not established as central to Krabbe disease.
gaps.caveat: The intervention is an experimental transcranial modality with limited evidence for sustained CNS delivery or disease-specific safety.
gaps.experiment: Perform a controlled ultrasound feasibility and dose-ranging study in a Krabbe disease mouse model with α-synuclein and demyelination endpoints.

"Surprisingly, psychosine levels were reduced to the same extent as the non-hydroxy-GalCer, even though 2-hydroxy-GalCer was not reduced" (PMID:34262084, P16)

gaps.rationale: Bortezomib corrects a lysosomal trafficking defect in MPS-plus fibroblasts but has no demonstrated effect on psychosine accumulation or the central pathology of Krabbe disease.
gaps.caveat: Proteasome inhibition can cause substantial toxicity and does not directly substitute for deficient GALC activity.
gaps.experiment: Test bortezomib in GALC-deficient patient-derived cells and assess psychosine, globoid-cell formation, and viability before any animal work.

mechanism_evidence: "Correction of GALC deficiency after gene therapy with AAV9-GALC led to the elimination of α-synuclein high-molecular-weight protein aggregates and thio-S+ amyloid inclusions in the brain throughout the animals’ lifespans." (PMID:30127535, P54)

"Aggregates of α-synuclein were found in neurons in the cortex, hippocampus, midbrain, striatum, and brainstem in the twitcher (TWI) mouse model of KD, as well as in the brain of affected human patients1,41." (PMID:30127535, P4)
intervention_evidence: "BAG956 significantly reverses characteristic PD phenotypes in α-syn preformed fibril models in vitro and in vivo by promoting autophagic clearance of pathological α-syn aggregates." (PMID:37339636, P2)

gaps.rationale: BAG956 promotes autophagic clearance of pathological α-synuclein, matching a documented but probably secondary feature of Krabbe disease.
gaps.caveat: The evidence is preclinical and focused on Parkinson’s disease models; BAG956 is not an established intervention for GALC deficiency.
gaps.experiment: Evaluate BAG956 in patient-derived GALC-deficient neural cultures and a Krabbe model for aggregate clearance, lysosomal function, and neuroprotection.

mechanism_evidence: "GALC deficiency causes toxic accumulation of psychosine in the plasma membrane of cells throughout the nervous system." (PMID:35333110, P4)
"Surprisingly, psychosine levels were reduced to the same extent as the non-hydroxy-GalCer, even though 2-hydroxy-GalCer was not reduced" (PMID:34262084, P16)

literature.query: (TITLE_ABS:"eliglustat") AND (TITLE_ABS:"Krabbe disease" OR TITLE_ABS:"diffuse globoid body sclerosis" OR TITLE_ABS:"galactocerebrosidase deficiency" OR TITLE_ABS:"galactosylceramidase deficiency" OR TITLE_ABS:"galactosylceramide lipidosis" OR TITLE_ABS:"GALC deficiency")

gaps.rationale: Eliglustat is a substrate-reduction drug with an approved safety precedent and could theoretically reduce upstream sphingolipid flux in GALC deficiency.
gaps.caveat: The quoted MPS-plus evidence concerns LacCer trafficking, not psychosine toxicity, and eliglustat does not replace GALC or reliably address nervous-system substrate pools.
gaps.experiment: Measure eliglustat effects on psychosine, psychosines-related storage, and neuronal function in patient-derived GALC-deficient cells followed by a preclinical model if justified.

papers.title: Ultrastructural Characterization of the Lower Motor System in a Mouse Model of Krabbe Disease.
papers.summary: Transmission electron microscopy of Twitcher mice shows that Krabbe disease progresses along the lower motor pathway, with severe distal axonal, Schwann-cell, neuromuscular-junction, and muscle abnormalities despite relatively preserved motor-neuron somata. The temporal and spatial pattern supports a dying-back, myelin-independent mechanism, while early muscle atrophy suggests a direct component of muscle toxicity that is not fully explained by denervation.
papers.why: The study supplies an experimentally characterized mouse model and ultrastructural assay revealing early peripheral and neuromuscular pathology relevant to Krabbe disease research.

papers.title: Pilot study of newborn screening for six lysosomal storage diseases using Tandem Mass Spectrometry.
papers.summary: The study demonstrates a 6-plex tandem mass spectrometry enzymatic activity assay for newborn screening of six lysosomal storage diseases, including Krabbe disease. For Krabbe disease, 11 of approximately 43,000 newborn dried blood spots had GALC activity below the screening cutoff, but none carried nucleotide changes consistent with a diagnosis of Krabbe disease; all contained one or more reported non-pathogenic GALC variants.
papers.why: The pilot study tested approximately 43,000 newborn dried-blood-spot specimens with a six-enzyme MS/MS assay that directly included GALC and identified screens for Krabbe disease.

papers.title: An Overview of PDE4 Inhibitors in Clinical Trials: 2010 to Early 2022.
papers.summary: This review identifies ibudilast as a PDE4 inhibitor marketed for Krabbe disease, also called globoid cell leukodystrophy. It connects this use to the broader mechanism of PDE4 inhibition, which increases intracellular cAMP, but it does not report new patient outcomes, mechanistic studies, or disease-specific treatment effects for Krabbe disease.
papers.why: The review explicitly identifies ibudilast, a PDE4 inhibitor, as a drug used for Krabbe disease and reviews its clinical-trial development.

papers.title: Consensus guidelines for newborn screening, diagnosis and treatment of infantile Krabbe disease.
papers.summary: This consensus review finds that newborn screening for Krabbe disease can identify infantile disease early enough for referral and presymptomatic human stem cell transplantation, which improves survival and neurologic function, especially when initiated within the first four weeks of life. It recommends primary dried-blood-spot GALC activity screening followed by psychosine measurement and/or comprehensive GALC molecular testing, with rapid confirmatory testing and referral because evidence for the very early treatment pathway remains largely case-series based and expert opinion.
papers.why: Provides actionable screening, confirmatory testing, referral, and transplantation guidelines supported by experience from Krabbe newborn-screening programs.

papers.title: Lysosomal Re-acidification Prevents Lysosphingolipid-Induced Lysosomal Impairment and Cellular Toxicity.
papers.summary: Psychosine and structurally related lysosphingolipids caused lysosomal alkalinization and multiple cellular defects in rat and human oligodendrocyte precursor cells, while several compounds prevented these effects by promoting lysosomal re-acidification. In twitcher mice with Krabbe disease, the CNS-penetrant compound NKH-477 normalized lysosomal pH, restored oligodendrocyte precursor division, preserved myelin, improved motor function and weight gain, and extended survival without reducing CNS psychosine burden or correcting the GALC mutation.
papers.why: Drug screens identified protective compounds that re-acidify lysosomes, and a CNS-penetrant agent improved myelin, oligodendrocyte progenitors, motor behavior, and lifespan in a mouse model of Krabbe disease.

papers.title: Combined gene/cell therapies provide long-term and pervasive rescue of multiple pathological symptoms in a murine model of globoid cell leukodystrophy.
papers.summary: In Twitcher mice with globoid cell leukodystrophy, neonatal GALC-overexpressing neural stem cell transplantation or lentiviral intracerebral gene therapy synergized with bone marrow transplant to markedly extend lifespan, improve clinical function, reduce toxic psychosine storage, and preserve CNS and peripheral nervous system myelination. Persistent astrogliosis, myelin-gene downregulation, residual peripheral dysfunction, and slowed nerve conduction showed that combined therapy did not fully normalize disease or prevent all progression.
papers.why: Early neonatal gene or neural stem-cell therapy synergized with bone marrow transplantation to provide long-term, widespread rescue in a murine model of globoid cell leukodystrophy.

papers.title: The mechanism of glycosphingolipid degradation revealed by a GALC-SapA complex structure.
papers.summary: Structural and mutagenesis experiments show that acidic, endolysosomal conditions promote formation of a 2:2 GALC–SapA heterotetramer whose open substrate channel can present galactocerebroside to GALC for degradation. Mutational analyses identify specific SapA interface residues required for GALC binding and demonstrate that SapB, SapD, and SapC do not detectably bind GALC under the tested conditions, explaining saposin specificity.
papers.why: The study directly resolves the GALC–SapA complex involved in Krabbe disease and provides a transferable structural framework for enzyme or chaperone-based strategies.

papers.title: Brain-targeted enzyme-loaded nanoparticles: A breach through the blood-brain barrier for enzyme replacement therapy in Krabbe disease.
papers.summary: Brain-targeted Ang2-, g7-, or Tf2-functionalized poly-(lactide-co-glycolide) nanoparticles carrying cross-linked GALC enzyme aggregates delivered active GALC to lysosomes in deficient fibroblasts and raised brain GALC activity to approximately the disease-free heterozygous level in Twitcher mice. The formulation did not significantly restore GALC activity in spinal cord, sciatic nerve, kidney, or liver to healthy levels, and no clinical efficacy was evaluated.
papers.why: The study develops brain-targeted GALC enzyme replacement nanoparticles and demonstrates recovery of nervous-system enzyme activity in the Twitcher mouse model of Krabbe disease.

papers.title: Neuroimmune mechanisms in Krabbe's disease.
papers.summary: This review concludes that GALC deficiency triggers early innate immune activation in Krabbe disease, with reactive microglia preceding astrocyte reactivation, cytokine elevation, oligodendrocyte dysfunction, and overt demyelination. It identifies inflammation-modulating and GALC-directed interventions with experimental or clinical benefit, while emphasizing that psychosine-dependent immune mechanisms and some immune-signaling pathways remain uncertain.
papers.why: The review documents an established Krabbe treatment—hematopoietic stem cell transplantation—and links its benefit to immune mechanisms while highlighting neuroinflammatory pathways that can guide additional therapies.

papers.title: A prospective natural history study of Krabbe disease in a patient cohort with onset between 6 months and 3 years of life.
papers.summary: This prospective natural-history cohort characterized clinical, developmental, neurophysiological, neuroradiological, and biochemical findings in 35 children with Krabbe disease onset between 6 and 36 months. Patients with onset at or before 12 months generally had more severe disease and faster progression than those with later onset, supporting revised infantile and late-infantile classifications and preliminary prognostic use of a severity index.
papers.why: This prospective Krabbe cohort provides standardized longitudinal clinical, neurophysiologic, imaging, biochemical, and genetic outcome measures useful for treatment trials and prognosis.

papers.title: Pervasive supply of therapeutic lysosomal enzymes in the CNS of normal and Krabbe-affected non-human primates by intracerebral lentiviral gene therapy.
papers.summary: Intracerebral delivery of a lentiviral vector encoding human GALC restored substantial GALC activity throughout the brain, spinal cord, and cerebrospinal fluid of one juvenile rhesus macaque with Krabbe disease and was accompanied by a preliminary improvement in motor performance. The treatment showed a favorable short-term safety profile with local inflammation but no detected off-target integration or molecular evidence of insertional genotoxicity, although efficacy and safety were evaluated in only one affected animal without long-term follow-up.
papers.why: Intracerebral lentiviral GALC delivery in Krabbe-affected macaques achieved widespread enzyme distribution, physiological GALC activity, preliminary benefit, and a favorable measured safety profile.

papers.title: Therapeutic benefit of lentiviral-mediated neonatal intracerebral gene therapy in a mouse model of globoid cell leukodystrophy.
papers.summary: A single neonatal intracerebral injection of the bidirectional lentiviral vector bdLV.GALC restored GALC activity across the CNS of Twitcher mice, reduced toxic substrate accumulation, ameliorated several histopathological abnormalities, and modestly prolonged survival. Treatment did not demonstrably improve demyelination and showed no detected tumor formation or substantial systemic vector distribution during the reported observation periods.
papers.why: Neonatal LV.GALC delivery in Twitcher mice restored CNS GALC activity, reduced psychosine and pathology, and improved lifespan.

papers.title: Peripheral neuropathy in the Twitcher mouse involves the activation of axonal caspase 3.
papers.summary: The Twitcher mouse model of Krabbe disease shows early abnormal myelination followed by axonal caspase 3 activation, peripheral demyelination, slowed motor conduction, and dying-back neuropathy. Psychosine directly and dose-dependently activates caspase 3 and induces DNA fragmentation in NSC34 motor neuronal cells without myelinating glia, supporting its sufficiency as a pathogenic mediator of axonal injury.
papers.why: The paper provides disease-specific mouse and in vitro models plus measurable axonal caspase-3 and psychosine phenotypes relevant to Krabbe research.

papers.title: Efficacy and Safety of a Krabbe Disease Gene Therapy.
papers.summary: This study shows that a single intracisterna magna administration of AAVhu68 expressing codon-optimized GALC improves survival, GALC activity, myelination, neurologic function, and neuroinflammation in Twitcher mice and Krabbe dogs. In juvenile rhesus macaques, the vector showed no dose-limiting toxicity, although sporadic minimal dorsal root ganglia neuronal degeneration and associated axonopathy occurred.
papers.why: The study demonstrates efficacy and initial safety of cisterna-magna AAV gene delivery in mouse, canine, and nonhuman-primate models of Krabbe disease.

papers.title: Brainstem development requires galactosylceramidase and is critical for pathogenesis in a model of Krabbe disease.
papers.summary: Conditional Galc deletion in mice identifies a critical postnatal P4–P6 window in which neuronal GALC is required for brainstem development, with deletion before P6 worsening psychosine accumulation, pathology, and survival. Neuron-specific Galc deletion causes persistent TBR1-positive immature brainstem neurons, demonstrating a cell-autonomous role for GALC in neuronal maturation that is not directly driven by neuronal psychosine accumulation.
papers.why: Develops and validates a timing-dependent GALC-deficient mouse model that identifies a critical perinatal window of brainstem vulnerability in Krabbe disease.

papers.title: α-Synuclein interacts directly but reversibly with psychosine: implications for α-synucleinopathies.
papers.summary: In GALC-deficient twitcher mice and human Krabbe disease brain tissue, accumulated psychosine associates with and promotes α-synuclein aggregation; genetic correction of GALC with AAV9-GALC prevents the aggregation, whereas SNCA deletion only mildly and temporarily improves neurological outcomes without correcting psychosine accumulation. Biophysical and cell experiments further show direct, cooperative psychosine binding to the α-synuclein C-terminus and inhibition of psychosine-induced aggregation by dopamine and carbidopa.
papers.why: Identifies dopamine and carbidopa as small molecules that reverse psychosine-induced alpha-synuclein structural changes while validating genetic GALC correction as an aggregation-preventing strategy.

papers.title: CRISPR/Cas9 Genome Engineering in Engraftable Human Brain-Derived Neural Stem Cells.
papers.summary: The study engineers banked human neural stem cells to overexpress GALC and enrich the targeted cells to more than 90%; these cells increased GALC activity in Krabbe disease fibroblasts in vitro through a mannose-6-phosphate-dependent mechanism. The engineered cells retained migration and neuronal, astrocytic, and oligodendrocytic differentiation in mice, but in vivo correction and therapeutic efficacy in a Krabbe disease model were not demonstrated.
papers.why: The study generated GALC-overexpressing gene-edited human neural stem cells and demonstrated migration, differentiation, and cross-correction of GALC activity after transplantation, directly supporting cell and gene therapy for Krabbe disease.

papers.title: Natural history of Krabbe disease - a nationwide study in Germany using clinical and MRI data.
papers.summary: A nationwide German observational cohort characterized the clinical, developmental, genetic, and MRI natural history of Krabbe disease across infantile, later-onset, adolescent, and adult forms. The study identified form-specific MRI patterns and quantitative tools for diagnosis and follow-up, while finding that age at onset and the available GALC genotype data did not reliably predict disease-course severity or progression.
papers.why: The study establishes disease-form definitions and standardized clinical/MRI trajectories across the Krabbe disease spectrum that can support diagnosis and future trial endpoint design.

papers.title: Fingolimod Rescues Demyelination in a Mouse Model of Krabbe's Disease.
papers.summary: Fingolimod treatment from postnatal day 21 improved cerebellar myelin-related pathology, reduced microglial and globoid-cell reactivity, improved mobility and twitching, and modestly increased survival in homozygous twitcher mice carrying a natural galc mutation. Effects were tissue- and marker-dependent: several myelin, axonal, and Purkinje-cell outcomes were unchanged, and peripheral sciatic-nerve demyelination was not corrected.
papers.why: In vivo fingolimod treatment in twitcher mice rescued myelin, reduced neurofilament damage, regulated astrocyte and microglial reactivity, and increased lifespan, directly demonstrating a drug therapy in a Krabbe disease model.

papers.title: Prion-like α-synuclein pathology in the brain of infants with Krabbe disease.
papers.summary: Post-mortem infant Krabbe disease brain tissue showed widespread α-synuclein accumulation and soluble, seed-competent α-synuclein that induced fibril formation by RT-QuIC, but lacked Lewy bodies and pS129-positive globoid cells. The findings suggest an early form of α-synuclein pathology associated with altered sphingolipid metabolism, although the small tissue cohort limits generalizability.
papers.why: The study demonstrates prion-like alpha-synuclein seeding in infant Krabbe brain tissue and thereby provides a disease-specific assay and mechanistic biomarker of pathological protein aggregation.

papers.title: Patient fibroblasts-derived induced neurons demonstrate autonomous neuronal defects in adult-onset Krabbe disease.
papers.summary: Patient fibroblasts directly converted into induced neurons reproduced reduced GALC activity, psychosine accumulation, lysosomal and mitochondrial abnormalities, neurite defects, and impaired mitochondrial membrane potential in two adult-onset Krabbe disease patients. Exposure of healthy control induced neurons to psychosine induced concentration-dependent lysosomal accumulation and recapitulated neurite and mitochondrial defects, supporting an autonomous, psychosine-mediated neuronal mechanism that is independent of myelin loss.
papers.why: Patient-derived induced neurons reproduced GALC deficiency, psychosine accumulation, lysosomal abnormalities, mitochondrial dysfunction, and neurite defects, while psychosine exposure reproduced key pathology in control neurons.

papers.title: Design of a regulated lentiviral vector for hematopoietic stem cell gene therapy of globoid cell leukodystrophy.
papers.summary: The paper develops a miR-126-regulated, codon-optimized lentiviral vector that limits human GALC expression in immature hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells while sustaining high enzyme activity in their differentiated progeny. The vector showed no detectable perturbation of human HSPC viability, clonogenicity, sphingolipid content, or engraftment, and transplantation of corrected Twitcher mouse HSPCs prolonged survival, reduced nervous-system sphingolipid storage and astrogliosis, and improved motor manifestations without halting disease progression.
papers.why: A regulated lentiviral vector safely expressed GALC in human HSPCs and corrected HSPC transplantation improved survival and phenotype in a murine GLD model.

papers.title: Revisiting magnetic resonance imaging pattern of Krabbe disease - Lessons from an Indian cohort.
papers.summary: This retrospective cohort of 27 patients found four age-associated MRI patterns in Krabbe disease, with early infantile and late infantile disease showing diffuse cerebral, cerebellar, and dentate-hilum involvement, while juvenile and adult disease more often showed corticospinal tract and posterior deep/periventricular white-matter involvement. MRI and CT supported diagnosis and differential diagnosis, while DTI, spectroscopy, and the Loes score emerged as possible tools for microstructural assessment and longitudinal outcome evaluation, although their prognostic value was not established.
papers.why: The cohort identifies four MRI patterns that distinguish Krabbe clinical subtypes and can inform diagnosis, prognostication, and longitudinal monitoring.

papers.title: Human iPSC-based neurodevelopmental models of globoid cell leukodystrophy uncover patient- and cell type-specific disease phenotypes.
papers.summary: Patient-derived GLD iPSC lines and their neuronal/glial progeny reproduce mutation-dependent psychosine storage, impaired neuronal and oligodendroglial differentiation, lipidomic abnormalities, and, in GLD5 cells, cellular senescence. LV-mediated GALC gene transfer normalizes or reduces psychosine and partially rescues differentiation, lipidome, and senescence phenotypes, while excessive GALC expression disrupts neural differentiation and indicates that dosage must be controlled.
papers.why: Directly models Krabbe disease in patient-derived neural cells and shows partial correction of pathological phenotypes by lentiviral GALC rescue.

papers.title: Transplantation of mouse embryonic stem cell-derived oligodendrocytes in the murine model of globoid cell leukodystrophy.
papers.summary: Mouse embryonic stem cells were differentiated into oligodendrocyte progenitor cells with relatively high GALC activity and greater resistance to psychosine toxicity than terminally differentiated oligodendrocytes. After bilateral forebrain transplantation into twitcher mice, poor graft survival, limited migration, and absent improvement in brain GALC activity, myelin basic protein, body weight, behavior, or life span showed that this treatment was insufficient to reverse globoid cell leukodystrophy.
papers.why: The study developed and tested a stem-cell-derived OPC transplantation protocol in twitcher mice, but poor survival and migration prevented improvement of GALC activity, myelination, lifespan, or behavior.

papers.title: Conditions for combining gene therapy with bone marrow transplantation in murine Krabbe disease.
papers.summary: In the GALC W339X twitcher mouse model of Krabbe disease, combining bone marrow transplantation with a single intravenous AAVrh10-mGALC injection markedly increased tissue GALC activity, restored sciatic-nerve myelination, and extended median survival from about 40 days to approximately 389–400 days. The benefit was dose- and timing-dependent: low vector doses, delayed treatment, and bone marrow from heterozygous donors reduced survival, while examination of more than 50 treated mice found no hepatic neoplastic changes.
papers.why: The study directly establishes dosing and timing conditions for combining bone marrow transplantation with AAVrh10-GALC therapy in a murine Krabbe disease model.

papers.title: Substrate reduction therapy for Krabbe disease and metachromatic leukodystrophy using a novel ceramide galactosyltransferase inhibitor.
papers.summary: The study identifies S202 as a potent, selective, brain-penetrant inhibitor of ceramide galactosyltransferase and shows that substrate reduction therapy lowers pathogenic lipids and modestly extends survival in GALC-deficient Twitcher mice. S202 also reduced sulfatide and lysosulfatide in an ARSA-deficient metachromatic leukodystrophy model, but chronic CGT inhibition caused dose-dependent peripheral and central nervous system toxicity in wild-type mice.
papers.why: The selective inhibitor S202 reduced galactosylceramide and psychosine and significantly extended lifespan in a mouse model of Krabbe disease.

papers.title: Newborn Screening for 6 Lysosomal Storage Disorders in China.
papers.summary: Tandem mass spectrometry newborn screening followed by molecular, psychosine, and clinical analysis identified nine newborns with Krabbe disease, all at risk for later-onset disease. GALC activity and psychosine measurements provided biochemical support, while GALC variants enabled molecular confirmation and subtype risk classification.
papers.why: The study validates a tandem-mass-spectrometry newborn-screening workflow that identified nine cases of Krabbe disease and subsequently characterized their clinical and biochemical forms.

papers.title: Pathogenic Variants in GALC Gene Correlate With Late Onset Krabbe Disease and Vision Loss: Case Series and Review of Literature.
papers.summary: This five-patient case series found that GALC variants p.Y319C and p.L634S can be associated with late-onset Krabbe disease presenting with severe vision impairment and abnormal visual evoked potentials before other major neurologic findings. In the single patient treated with hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, vision and VEP changes stabilized during 12 months of follow-up, but the small retrospective uncontrolled series cannot establish efficacy.
papers.why: The case series identifies genotype-associated visual phenotypes and supports VEP/ERG surveillance and transplant follow-up in late-onset Krabbe disease.

papers.title: Regional differences in fiber tractography predict neurodevelopmental outcomes in neonates with infantile Krabbe disease.
papers.summary: In nine neonates with early-infantile Krabbe disease, quantitative diffusion tensor imaging identified reduced fractional anisotropy and increased mean and radial diffusivity in six white-matter tracts before symptoms and correlated regional microstructural abnormalities with later neurodevelopmental outcomes after umbilical cord blood transplantation. The findings support DTI as an early prognostic biomarker and screening component, whereas modified Loes scores did not correlate with the quantitative DTI findings or functional outcomes.
papers.why: The study validates quantitative DTI tractography in presymptomatic infants with Krabbe disease and shows that regional white-matter measures predict post-transplant cognitive and motor outcomes.

papers.title: Preclinical studies in Krabbe disease: A model for the investigation of novel combination therapies for lysosomal storage diseases.
papers.summary: This review summarizes preclinical findings in Krabbe disease, emphasizing GALC deficiency, psychosine accumulation, demyelination, and globoid-cell pathology as key disease mechanisms. It reports that substrate reduction therapy, hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation, enzyme replacement, and AAV-based gene therapy—especially combination regimens—improve survival and disease-associated pathology in mouse and canine models, but each has important limitations including incomplete efficacy, blood-brain barrier delivery, toxicity, and declining long-term AAV efficacy.
papers.why: The review summarizes developed preclinical gene-therapy and substrate-reduction strategies, including approaches already entering Krabbe disease trials.

papers.title: Allogeneic Cell Therapy Applications in Neonates: A Systematic Review.
papers.summary: This systematic review identifies neonatal allogeneic umbilical cord blood-derived total nucleated cell transplantation as a possible treatment approach for Krabbe disease, but the evidence is limited to small, uncontrolled studies. Favorable neurological outcomes were reported alongside substantial graft-versus-host disease, mortality, and persistent spasticity, with no controlled assessment establishing efficacy.
papers.why: The systematic review includes treatment data from 13 infants with Krabbe disease and reports feasibility and safety outcomes for allogeneic cell therapy, including graft-versus-host disease with cord-blood-derived cells.

papers.title: Galactosylceramidase deficiency and pathological abnormalities in cerebral white matter of Krabbe disease.
papers.summary: Postmortem brain analysis showed that Krabbe disease severity was associated with GALC deficiency, psychosine accumulation, severe loss of mature myelin, increased ASAH1 and LAMP1, and increased globoid cells, astrogliosis, and CD8-positive T lymphocytes. The study also supports GALC protein quantification as a potential discriminator of genotype and disease onset and identifies multiple sclerosis as a mechanistically relevant source of transferable therapeutic strategies.
papers.why: The paper develops sensitive GALC detection and quantitative psychosine/pathology assays and validates them in Krabbe brain tissue.

papers.title: Prosaposin deficiency and saposin B deficiency (activator-deficient metachromatic leukodystrophy): report on two patients detected by analysis of urinary sphingolipids and carrying novel PSAP gene mutations.
papers.summary: The paper reports two patients with novel PSAP variants causing prosaposin deficiency and isolated saposin B deficiency, characterized by lysosomal sphingolipid storage, neurovisceral or leukodystrophic phenotypes, and distinctive urinary lipid abnormalities. For Krabbe disease research, the paper explicitly links isolated saposin A deficiency to Krabbe leukodystrophy and reports reduced galactosylceramide beta-galactosidase activity in prosaposin-deficient fibroblasts.
papers.why: The study validates urinary sphingolipid profiling and mass spectrometry as diagnostic methods for saposin-related sphingolipidoses with leukodystrophy phenotypes relevant to Krabbe disease.

papers.title: Gene therapy for the leukodystrophies: From preclinical animal studies to clinical trials.
papers.summary: This review identifies globoid cell leukodystrophy (GLD), also called Krabbe disease, as a lysosomal leukodystrophy caused by GALC mutations and toxic psychosine accumulation. It describes preclinical and clinical AAV-GALC gene-therapy approaches, including FBX101 and intracisterna magna AAVhu68-GALC, while emphasizing neuroinflammation, limited therapeutic efficacy of some monotherapies, and the need for long-term safety monitoring.
papers.why: The review directly includes globoid cell leukodystrophy and summarizes tested gene-delivery, transplantation, dosing, delivery-route, and monitoring strategies.

papers.title: Newborn Screening for Krabbe Disease-Illinois Experience: Role of Psychosine in Diagnosis of the Disease.
papers.summary: In a statewide observational newborn-screening program, psychosine measurement reduced false-positive interpretation of low GALC activity and enabled timely identification of two infants with infantile Krabbe disease and six suspected late-onset cases. Both infants treated with human stem cell transplantation were doing well with mild developmental delays, but the evidence is observational and based on very few confirmed cases.
papers.why: Population screening data show that psychosine measurement reduces GALC pseudodeficiency false positives and enables timely diagnosis of Krabbe disease.

papers.title: Benefits of newborn screening and hematopoietic cell transplant in infantile Krabbe disease.
papers.summary: This retrospective series of six infants with infantile Krabbe disease detected by expanded newborn screening found that all received hematopoietic cell transplantation before 6 weeks of age, engrafted donor cells, and remained alive with normal GALC levels. HCT was associated with survival and ongoing developmental and neurologic gains, but persistent developmental delay, motor impairment, neuropathy, and incomplete psychosine normalization remained; an investigational intrathecal oligodendrocyte-like-cell protocol did not appear to provide additional clinical benefit.
papers.why: This report directly demonstrates that early hematopoietic cell transplantation in newborns with infantile Krabbe disease can achieve engraftment and developmental or neurologic benefit.

papers.title: The Pathogenic Sphingolipid Psychosine is Secreted in Extracellular Vesicles in the Brain of a Mouse Model of Krabbe Disease.
papers.summary: The study shows that a fraction of psychosine in the Twitcher mouse brain is secreted in brain-derived extracellular vesicles, with EV-associated psychosine increasing during disease progression. Pharmacologic attenuation of EV release with the neutral sphingomyelinase 2 inhibitor GW4869 reduced brain ceramides and EVs but unexpectedly accelerated early disease signs without significantly changing established demyelination or gliosis measures.
papers.why: This study uses the twitcher Krabbe model to test EV-pathway modulation and measure psychosine-associated neuropathology and disease severity.

papers.title: Neuron-specific ablation of the Krabbe disease gene galactosylceramidase in mice results in neurodegeneration.
papers.summary: Pan-neuronal deletion of Galc in mice was sufficient to produce psychosine accumulation, neuronal and axonal degeneration, neuroinflammation, motor deficits, and mild CNS myelin loss, despite limited peripheral pathology and no reduced lifespan. The findings support a neuron-autonomous contribution of GALC deficiency to Krabbe disease, while indicating that nonneuronal GALC deficiency is needed for the full disease phenotype.
papers.why: The novel neuron-specific Galc knockout mouse directly models a neuron-autonomous disease mechanism and provides an in vivo system for testing GALC-directed interventions.

papers.title: Newborn Screening for Krabbe Disease: Status Quo and Recommendations for Improvements.
papers.summary: This paper finds that using psychosine (PSY) as a second-tier newborn-screening test after reduced GALC activity can virtually eliminate false-positive results while retaining high sensitivity for infantile and late-infantile Krabbe disease. Increasing the PSY cutoff improves specificity but progressively risks missing later-onset cases, and the paper also documents short-term outcomes of 11 infantile cases identified through screening, including hematopoietic stem cell transplantation.
papers.why: Reports validated Krabbe newborn-screening workflows and data showing how optimized psychosine cutoffs can reduce false positives while preserving sensitivity.

papers.title: Hematopoietic Stem cell transplantation and lentiviral vector-based gene therapy for Krabbe's disease: Present convictions and future prospects.
papers.summary: In the twitcher mouse model of Krabbe disease, stronger busulfan conditioning prolonged hematopoietic stem and progenitor cell transplantation-associated survival, but bone-marrow engraftment did not explain the outcome. A GALC-ApoE receptor-binding-domain fusion protein was efficiently taken up by GALC-deficient human fibroblasts through an M6P-independent route, yet lentiviral delivery of this protein to donor HSPC did not improve survival at the tested vector copy number, indicating a major biodistribution or uptake barrier to cross-correction.
papers.why: The paper provides experimental and review evidence for HSC transplantation, conditioning optimization, lentiviral GALC gene therapy, and a fusion-protein strategy to improve GALC delivery in Krabbe disease.

papers.title: Rapamycin Alleviates Protein Aggregates, Reduces Neuroinflammation, and Rescues Demyelination in Globoid Cell Leukodystrophy.
papers.summary: In twitcher mice, rapamycin inhibited mTOR signaling, reduced insoluble protein aggregates and reactive astrocyte/microglia phenotypes, and partially preserved cortical myeloarchitecture and lifespan. Effects on body weight and several aggregate or myelin measurements were absent or limited, and the authors propose rapamycin as a complementary rather than complete treatment for Krabbe disease.
papers.why: Rapamycin is tested in the twitcher mouse model of globoid cell leukodystrophy and reduces aggregates, neuroinflammation, demyelination, and pathology while extending survival.

papers.title: The Impact of Post-Analytical Tools on New York Screening for Krabbe Disease and Pompe Disease.
papers.summary: In New York newborn screening, integrating GALC activity with additional lysosomal enzyme activities, C26:0-LPC, covariates, and CLIR pattern-recognition tools substantially reduced repeat testing, molecular testing, and referrals while preserving a similar number of possible Krabbe disease cases. The study was observational, and the authors characterized the absence of apparently missed cases as circumstantial rather than definitive.
papers.why: The optimized screening algorithm reduced Krabbe disease referrals by almost 80% while directly improving newborn screening performance.

papers.title: CRISPR-Cas9 Knock-In of T513M and G41S Mutations in the Murine β-Galactosyl-Ceramidase Gene Re-capitulates Early-Onset and Adult-Onset Forms of Krabbe Disease.
papers.summary: The paper generated two CRISPR-Cas9 GALC knock-in mouse lines that model contrasting forms of Krabbe disease: GALC T513M/T513M mice develop severe infantile disease with absent brain GALC activity, psychosine accumulation, rapid demyelination, neurological deterioration and early death, whereas GALC G41S/G41S mice develop milder adult-onset disease with residual GALC activity, little psychosine accumulation and late central demyelination. The models also show variant-dependent lysosomal trafficking, autophagy and behavioral differences and are proposed for mechanistic and preclinical therapeutic studies.
papers.why: The new mouse lines reproduce infantile and adult-onset Krabbe phenotypes and enable mutation-specific studies of GALC trafficking and disease progression.

papers.title: Neurodegenerative Disorder Risk in Krabbe Disease Carriers.
papers.summary: Comparative whole-brain proteomics showed that heterozygous galc +/− mice have a proteomic profile distinct from homozygous twitcher and wild-type mice despite an apparently normal phenotype. The altered proteoforms implicate cytoskeletal and myelin dynamics, proteostasis, lipid metabolism, mitochondrial integrity, and energy supply, suggesting possible but unconfirmed neurological vulnerability in Krabbe disease carriers.
papers.why: The study reports disease- and carrier-associated proteomic alterations that supply measurable targets for studying Krabbe neurodegeneration.

papers.title: Human iPSC-derived astrocytes generated from donors with globoid cell leukodystrophy display phenotypes associated with disease.
papers.summary: Human iPSC-derived astrocytes from two infantile-onset Krabbe disease donors reproduced disease-associated psychosine accumulation, inflammatory and lipid-biosynthesis changes, and reduced survival of neurons cocultured with them. Inhibiting glucosylceramide synthase or serine palmitoyltransferase reduced sphingolipids but did not rescue neuronal survival, indicating that elevated compensatory lipids were not sufficient to explain the astrocyte-mediated toxicity.
papers.why: It provides a patient-specific cellular disease model and experimentally tests two substrate-reduction strategies, while revealing astrocyte-mediated neurotoxicity as a potential target.

papers.title: Reduction in miR-219 expression underlies cellular pathogenesis of oligodendrocytes in a mouse model of Krabbe disease.
papers.summary: The paper shows that miR-219 expression and functional activity are reduced in developing oligodendrocytes from twitcher mice, a mouse model of Krabbe disease. Exogenous miR-219 partially reduced psychosine accumulation and rescued oligodendrocyte differentiation, myelin-marker expression, and apoptotic cell death in cultured twitcher oligodendrocytes, supporting its therapeutic potential but not yet establishing in vivo or clinical efficacy.
papers.why: Exogenous miR-219 rescued developmental defects, reduced psychosine accumulation, and suppressed apoptosis in oligodendrocyte precursor cells isolated from a Krabbe mouse model.

papers.title: A Roadmap for Potential Improvement of Newborn Screening for Inherited Metabolic Diseases Following Recent Developments and Successful Applications of Bivariate Normal Limits for Pre-Symptomatic Detection of MPS I, Pompe Disease, and Krabbe Disease.
papers.summary: This review reports that a bivariate normal limits newborn-screening method combining low galactocerebrosidase activity and high psychosine in dried blood spots can pre-symptomatically identify infants likely to have early-onset Krabbe disease and benefit from hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. Retrospective performance estimates were excellent, but prospective validation was still underway and implementation may be affected by laboratory measurement differences.
papers.why: The review reports successful bivariate-normal-limit newborn screening that combines GALC and psychosine activity to identify presymptomatic Krabbe disease, while noting psychosine-related false positives.

papers.title: Establishment of Cutoff Values for Newborn Screening of Six Lysosomal Storage Disorders by Tandem Mass Spectrometry.
papers.summary: The study shows that tandem mass spectrometry of dried blood spots can screen newborns for Krabbe disease through reduced GALC enzyme activity, with five children confirmed by genetic testing among 38,945 screened newborns. Batch-specific cutoffs based on 20% of median GALC activity were considered feasible, but seasonal enzyme-activity variation and the need for larger cohorts limit fixed-cutoff and performance estimates.
papers.why: The study establishes a large-scale newborn-screening workflow and directly identifies five infants with Krabbe disease using GALC activity measurement followed by genetic confirmation.

papers.title: Human iPSC-derived myelinating organoids and globoid cells to study Krabbe disease.
papers.summary: Patient-derived iPSC cultures provide two complementary in-vitro models of Krabbe disease: myelinating organoids that reproduce early myelin abnormalities and intrinsic, inflammation-independent demyelination, and GalCer-fed microglia that form pathognomonic globoid cells with transient lysosomal and autophagy perturbations. The study also finds preserved neurogenesis, astrogenesis, oligodendrogenesis, and proliferation, while identifying limited maintenance of myelin during prolonged culture and the absence of isogenic controls as model limitations.
papers.why: Develops and validates patient-derived iPSC organoid and microglial models that reproduce early demyelination and globoid-cell phenotypes.

papers.title: Safety, Tolerability, Pharmacokinetics, and Preliminary Efficacy of PLX-200 in Pediatric Patients (Master Protocol)
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the safety, tolerability and clinical activity of PLX-200 in pediatric patients with lysosomal storage disorders.

papers.title: Human Placental-Derived Stem Cell Transplantation
papers.summary: The purpose of this clinical trial is to investigate the safety of human placental-derived stem cells (HPDSC) given in conjunction with umbilical cord blood (UCB) stem cells in patients with various malignant or nonmalignant disorders who require a stem cell transplant. Patients will get either full dose (high-intensity) or lower dose (low intensity) chemo- and immunotherapy followed by a stem cell transplantation with UCB and HPDSC.

papers.title: Allogeneic Bone Marrow Transplant for Inherited Metabolic Disorders
papers.summary: Rationale: Chemotherapy administration before a donor stem cell transplant is necessary to stop the patient's immune system from rejecting the donor's stem cells. When healthy stem cells from a donor are infused into the patient, the donor white blood cells can provide the missing enzyme that causes the metabolic disease. Sometimes the transplanted cells from a donor can make an immune response against the body's normal cells. Giving a monoclonal antibody, alemtuzumab, before transplant and cyclosporine and mycophenolate mofetil before and after transplant may stop this from happening. This ma

papers.title: UCB Transplant of Inherited Metabolic Diseases With Administration of Intrathecal UCB Derived Oligodendrocyte-Like Cells
papers.summary: The primary objective of the study is to determine the safety and feasibility of intrathecal administration of DUOC-01 in patients who are undergoing standard treatment with umbilical cord blood transplant (UCBT) for inborn errors of metabolism and who have evidence of early demyelinating disease in the central nervous system (CNS). The secondary objective of the study is to describe the efficacy of UCBT with intrathecal administration of DUOC-01 in these patients.

papers.title: Reduced Intensity Conditioning for Non-Malignant Disorders Undergoing UCBT, BMT or PBSCT
papers.summary: The objective of this study is to evaluate the efficacy of using a reduced-intensity condition (RIC) regimen with umbilical cord blood transplant (UCBT), double cord UCBT, matched unrelated donor (MUD) bone marrow transplant (BMT) or peripheral blood stem cell transplant (PBSCT) in patients with non-malignant disorders that are amenable to treatment with hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HSCT). After transplant, subjects will be followed for late effects and for ongoing graft success.

papers.title: MT2013-31: Allo HCT for Metabolic Disorders and Severe Osteopetrosis
papers.summary: This single-institution, phase II study is designed to test the ability to achieve donor hematopoietic engraftment while maintaining low rates of transplant-related mortality (TRM) using busulfan- and fludarabine-based conditioning regimens with busulfan therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) for patients with various inherited metabolic disorders (IMD) and severe osteopetrosis (OP).

papers.title: MGTA-456 in Patients With Inherited Metabolic Disorders Undergoing Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation (HSCT)
papers.summary: This study is designed to assess the safety and efficacy of using MGTA-456 in patients with Inherited Metabolic Disorders (IMD) undergoing stem cell transplantation.

papers.title: Gene Transfer Clinical Trial for Infantile and Late Infantile Krabbe Disease Treated Previously With HSCT
papers.summary: This is a non-blinded, non-randomized dose escalation study of intravenous FBX-101 in which subjects will receive a single infusion of an adeno-associated virus gene therapy product, after more than 21 days of the HSCT (UCBT preferred HSCT source). Data from previously transplanted patients with infantile and late infantile Krabbe disease will be used as a comparator group.

papers.title: Study of Safety, Tolerability and Efficacy of PBKR03 in Pediatric Subjects With Early Infantile Krabbe Disease
papers.summary: PBKR03 is a gene therapy for Krabbe Disease (Globoid cell leukodystrophy) intended to deliver a functional copy of the GALC gene to the brain and peripheral tissues. This study will evaluate the safety, tolerability and efficacy of this treatment by first evaluating two different doses in two different age groups, then confirming the optimal dose to be used for confirmation of safety and efficacy.

papers.title: Reduced-Intensity Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplant for High Risk Lysosomal and Peroxisomal Disorders
papers.summary: This study is designed to test the ability to achieve donor hematopoietic engraftment while maintaining low rates of transplant-related mortality (TRM) in patients with high-risk lysosomal and peroxisomal disorders using a novel conditioning regimen for hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT). After a reduced-intensity conditioning regimen using volumetric-modulated arc therapy (VMAT)-delivered low-dose total body irradiation (TBI) with highly conformal marrow boosting, patients will be transplanted using either a related or unrelated allograft. The cell source may be marrow, peripheral blood

papers.title: Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation (HCT) for Inborn Errors of Metabolism
papers.summary: The primary objective of this clinical trial is to evaluate the ability to achieve and sustain donor engraftment in patients with lysosomal and peroxisomal inborn errors of metabolism undergoing hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HCT).

papers.title: Phase I/II Pilot Study of Mixed Chimerism to Treat Inherited Metabolic Disorders
papers.summary: The goal of this research study is to establish chimerism and avoid graft-versus-host-disease (GVHD) in patients with inherited metabolic disorders.

papers.title: Stem Cell Transplant for Inborn Errors of Metabolism
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to determine the safety and engraftment of donor hematopoietic cells using this conditioning regimen in patients undergoing a hematopoietic (blood forming) cell transplant for an inherited metabolic storage disease.

papers.title: HSCT for High Risk Inherited Inborn Errors
papers.summary:
