Hematopoietic stem cell transplantation has proven effective therapy for individuals with adrenoleukodystrophy (ALD), metachromatic leukodystrophy (MLD) or globoid cell leukodystrophy (GLD, or Krabbe disease). This protocol also considers other inherited metabolic diseases such as, but not limited to, GM1 gangliosidosis, Tay Sachs disease, Sanfilippo syndrome or Sandhoff disease, I-cell disease (mucolipidosis II).

For patients with advanced or rapidly progressive disease, the morbidity and mortality with transplantation is unacceptably high. Unfortunately, there are no viable alternative ther

papers.title: ALD-101 Adjuvant Therapy of Unrelated Umbilical Cord Blood Transfusion (UCBT) in Patients With Inherited Metabolic Diseases
papers.summary:
Eligible research subjects will receive an unrelated umbilical cord blood transfusion as a possible cure for their inherited metabolic disease. A portion of cord blood cells (ALD-101) will be separated from the cord blood unit and given approximately 4 hours after the standard cord blood transfusion.

The study will test if the supplemental cells will increase the speed at which normal levels of circulating blood cells are re-established after transplant.

papers.title: Open Targets drug and clinical candidates for Krabbe disease
AAV-Mediated GALC Gene Therapy Rescues Alpha-Synucleinopathy in the Spinal Cord of a Leukodystrophic Lysosomal Storage Disease Mouse Model.
papers.summary: This study identifies progressive thioflavin-S-positive inclusions containing alpha-synuclein in spinal neurons of twitcher mice and two terminal-stage human Krabbe disease cases, with early ventral predominance associated with regional psychosine levels. Neonatal combined intracranial, intravenous, and intrathecal AAV9-GALC gene therapy restored spinal GALC activity, reduced psychosine, and prevented the inclusions, whereas bone marrow transplantation alone did not significantly improve inclusion burden or GALC activity.

papers.title: Distinguishing the differences in β-glycosylceramidase folds, dynamics, and actions informs therapeutic uses.
papers.summary: The paper compares the structures, activities, dynamics, and binding-site stabilization of several β-glycosidases, including GALC, glucocerebrosidase, cytosolic β-glucosidase, lactase-phlorizin hydrolase, and membrane-bound glucosylceramidase. It also identifies recombinant glycosidases, glucosylceramide metabolism modulators, enzyme replacement therapies, and activity-based probes as established or emerging therapeutic and diagnostic approaches.

papers.title: Haploinsufficiency of lysosomal enzyme genes in Alzheimer’s disease
papers.summary: The paper reports that heterozygous loss-of-function variants in GALC and four other lysosomal enzyme genes alter Alzheimer’s disease-related amyloid biology in mice and that GALC variants are enriched among Alzheimer’s disease patients. The study directly implicates GALC in increased brain interstitial fluid Aβ40 and increased plaque formation, but its gene-therapy rescue experiments target PPT1 rather than GALC.

papers.title: The lysosomal disease caused by mutant VPS33A.
papers.summary: The paper identifies a VPS33A p.Arg498Trp MPS plus syndrome characterized by endosomal/lysosomal dysfunction, impaired lactosylceramide trafficking, and increased galactosylsphingosine. Bortezomib partially corrected lactosylceramide trafficking, while 50 nM eliglustat improved it in patient-derived fibroblasts, but neither intervention was shown to lower galactosylsphingosine or treat Krabbe disease.

papers.title: Prosaposin deficiency: further characterization of the sphingolipid activator protein-deficient sibs. Multiple glycolipid elevations (including lactosylceramidosis), partial enzyme deficiencies and ultrastructure of the skin in this generalized sphingolipid storage disease.
papers.summary: Prosaposin deficiency caused broad tissue accumulation of multiple sphingolipids, reduced beta-galactocerebrosidase activity, and produced massive lysosomal storage, with particularly strong elevations of glucosylceramide and lactosylceramide. The paper reports no intervention and does not report measurement or modulation of galactosylsphingosine.

papers.title: Sphingolipids and lysosomal pathologies.
papers.summary: This review states that defects in sphingolipid-degrading enzymes or sphingolipid activator proteins can cause accumulation of cytotoxic lysosphingolipids, including galactosylsphingosine, and that prosaposin feeding reverses membrane storage in patients with prosaposin deficiency. It proposes that SAP-assisted degradation occurs on inner endolysosomal membranes and is stimulated by anionic membrane lipids.

papers.title: Glucosylceramide modulates endolysosomal pH in Gaucher disease.
papers.summary: In cultured RAW macrophages and Gaucher patient lymphoblasts, increased glucosylceramide was associated with higher endolysosomal pH, while inhibiting glucosylceramide synthesis produced the same pH-related changes. Glucosylsphingosine reversed these effects, whereas the paper’s transfer target, galactosylsphingosine, did not, indicating that this rescue was specific and was not demonstrated in Krabbe disease cells.

papers.title: Substrate specificities of the two genetically distinct human brain beta-galactosidases.
papers.summary: The study separated two genetically distinct human brain beta-galactosidases and characterized their substrate specificities under different assay conditions. The authors report that optimized assays could diagnose the two genetic diseases caused by beta-galactosidase deficiencies in whole tissues, while tissue-dependent enzyme distributions may affect glycosphingolipid degradation in vivo.

papers.title: Lyso-glycosphingolipids mobilize calcium from brain microsomes via multiple mechanisms.
papers.summary: The study found that galactosylsphingosine and other lyso-glycosphingolipids mobilize calcium from rat brain microsomes, but by different calcium-release mechanisms. Galactosylsphingosine acted as a ryanodine receptor agonist, did not affect release through the inositol trisphosphate receptor or sarcoplasmic/endoplasmic reticulum Ca2+-ATPase, and reversed thapsigargin-induced inhibition of the latter enzyme.

papers.title: Intracellular cholesterol transport inhibition Impairs autophagy flux by decreasing autophagosome-lysosome fusion.
papers.summary: In RPE1 cells, lysosomal cholesterol accumulation induced by U18666A or bafilomycin A1 impaired autophagosome–lysosome fusion and STX17 trafficking independently of lysosomal pH. Methyl-β-cyclodextrin cleared accumulated cholesterol and restored fusion, but restored autophagy flux only when lysosomal acidification remained intact; bafilomycin A1 ultimately prevented flux restoration by increasing lysosomal pH.

papers.title: Nucleolipid Acid-Based Nanocarriers Restore Neuronal Lysosomal Acidification Defects.
papers.summary: The paper reports that succinic-acid-bearing nucleolipids formulated in oil-in-water nanoemulsions restored abnormally elevated lysosomal pH in ATP13A2-depleted human dopaminergic neuroblastoma cells. The 20-carbon formulation NE-8-3% fully restored lysosomal acidity at an active-substance concentration of 40 µM without detected cytotoxicity, but efficacy in animals, crossing of the blood-brain barrier, and efficacy in patients remain untested.

papers.title: Fronto-temporal dementia risk gene TMEM106B has opposing effects in different lysosomal storage disorders.
papers.summary: In lysosomal storage disease models, TMEM106B depletion reduced enhanced lysosomal pH and protected against selected GCase-inhibition phenotypes, whereas it worsened the lysosomal pH deficit caused by PPT1 deficiency and accelerated neurodegeneration. TMEM106B/V-ATPase modulation is therefore a context-dependent therapeutic mechanism, with the direction of benefit depending on the disease-specific V-ATPase and lysosomal pH state.

papers.title: Oral Delivery of the P2Y12 Receptor Antagonist Ticagrelor Prevents Loss of Photoreceptors in an ABCA4-/- Mouse Model of Retinal Degeneration.
papers.summary: In light-accelerated ABCA4−/− mice modeling Stargardt’s retinal degeneration, oral ticagrelor protected photoreceptor function and survival, consistent with enhanced lysosomal function. Ticagrelor lowered lysosomal pH in retinal pigment epithelial cells, reduced LAMP1 expression, and did not cause retinal bleeding during prolonged treatment.

papers.title: Plasma exosomes impair microglial degradation of α-synuclein through V-ATPase subunit V1G1.
papers.summary: In Parkinson's disease models, patient-derived plasma exosomes reduced microglial ATP6V1G1, increased lysosomal pH, impaired lysosomal enzyme activity and α-synuclein degradation, and promoted α-synuclein accumulation and inflammation. ATP6V1G1 knockdown reproduced cellular defects, whereas lentiviral ATP6V1G1 overexpression partly protected mice from MPTP-induced motor and dopaminergic neuronal damage, providing an experimentally supported strategy for targeting lysosomal pH homeostasis.

papers.title: Two lysosomal genes ATP13A2 and GBA1 interact to drive neurodegeneration.
papers.summary: In a Drosophila model combining partial neuronal loss of anne/ATP13A2 with partial glial loss of Gba1b/GBA1, the paper shows progressive impairment of lysosomal acidification, glucosylceramide accumulation, and neurodegeneration. ML-SA1, myriocin, and DFMO rescue selected neuronal or retinal phenotypes, supporting lysosomal trafficking, sphingolipid synthesis, and polyamine regulation as intervention points.

papers.title: N-Acetylcysteine Reverses the Mitochondrial Dysfunction Induced by Very Long-Chain Fatty Acids in Murine Oligodendrocyte Model of Adrenoleukodystrophy.
papers.summary: In an immortalized murine 158 N oligodendrocyte model exposed to hexacosanoic acid, the paper demonstrates mitochondrial dysfunction characterized by mitochondrial glutathione depletion, mitochondrial superoxide accumulation, reduced inner membrane potential, and reduced ATP production. N-acetylcysteine partially reverses these mitochondrial defects and improves cell survival under an additional acrolein insult, supporting metabolic antioxidant therapy for X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy and potentially transferable disorders involving similar mitochondrial vulnerability.

papers.title: Glycyrrhizic Acid Attenuates Aβ<sub>42</sub>-Induced Neurodegeneration Through Coordinated Regulation of Oxidative Stress, Synaptic Markers, and Key Alzheimer's Signaling Pathways.
papers.summary: In an Aβ42-induced IMR-32 cell model of Alzheimer’s disease, glycyrrhizic acid reduced oxidative stress, restored proteins associated with mitochondrial homeostasis, and reduced apoptosis. The study provides in vitro evidence for targeting mitochondrial dysfunction, but did not directly establish the relevant causal pathway or demonstrate efficacy in animals or humans.

papers.title: Resveratrol Analogs Ameliorate Mitochondrial Impairment and Insulin Resistance in a Streptozotocin-Induced In Vitro Model of Alzheimer's Disease.
papers.summary: In a streptozotocin-induced SH-SY5Y model of Alzheimer’s disease, the paper shows that resveratrol and three structural analogs restore insulin responsiveness, restore insulin-induced inhibitory phosphorylation of GSK-3β, and reduce amyloid-like protein aggregation. The compounds have distinct, structure-dependent effects on reactive oxygen species, autophagy, and mitochondrial membrane potential, with trimethyl resveratrol showing mitochondrial protection and strong autophagy induction despite little antioxidant activity.

papers.title: Neuroprotective Potential of <i>Sesamum indicum</i> in a Multifactorial In Vitro Neuron-Astrocyte System Exposed to Chronic Stress Mediators.
papers.summary: The paper reports that a Sesamum indicum whole paste extract (SIPE) reduced TGC-induced mitochondrial dysfunction in neuron–astrocyte-like co-cultures and 3D spheroids, preserving mitochondrial metabolic activity and membrane potential while suppressing mitochondrial superoxide. The effects were reproduced in 2D and 3D in vitro systems, but Krabbe disease, patient-derived systems, and clinical efficacy were not tested.

papers.title: Peptide-targeted cubosome and hexosome nanoassemblies mitigate mitochondrial dysfunction in a MitoPark model.
papers.summary: Intranasal peptide-functionalized, PUFA-enriched liquid crystalline lipid nanoparticles produced molecular, histological, and transcriptomic evidence of mitigation of mitochondrial dysfunction and neurodegeneration in the MitoPark model of Parkinson’s disease, particularly with antioxidant-loaded LNP2. However, the study found no statistically significant improvement in lifespan, motor performance, olfactory performance, or ATP5A1 expression, so functional benefit remained unproven.

papers.title: Lineage-tailored vesicles from human retinal ganglion-like cells drive metabolic homeostasis and bioenergetic recovery in glaucoma.
papers.summary: The paper shows that small extracellular vesicles derived from differentiated human retinal ganglion-like cells reduce mitochondrial stress, restore mitochondrial-glycolytic coupling, and preserve neuronal structure and survival in retinal ganglion-like cell cultures and an ocular hypertension mouse model of glaucoma. Untargeted metabolomic profiling and functional bioenergetic analysis associate the neuroprotection with metabolic reprogramming across oxidative phosphorylation, amino acid utilization, lipid metabolism, and redox regulation.

papers.title: Clinically advanced NLRP3 inhibitor modulates microglial transcriptome and alleviates α-synuclein-induced progression of parkinsonism.
papers.summary: This paper shows that chronic oral dapansutrile, a selective NLRP3 inhibitor, crosses the blood–brain barrier and suppresses NLRP3-associated neuroinflammation in mouse models of Parkinson’s disease and multiple system atrophy. Treatment reduced α-synuclein pathology and glial activation, protected nigral and striatal neurons, improved motor performance, and decreased plasma IL-18 and neurofilament light chain.

papers.title: Exidavnemab binds to aggregated α-synuclein in human brains affected by α-synucleinopathies.
papers.summary: In human post-mortem brain tissue, exidavnemab selectively bound pathological α-synuclein inclusions from Parkinson’s disease, Parkinson’s disease dementia, dementia with Lewy bodies, and multiple system atrophy, and immunodepleted aggregated and pSer129 α-synuclein from tissue extracts. These ex vivo data support target engagement but do not demonstrate therapeutic benefit in patients or establish applicability to Krabbe disease.

papers.title: Ultrasonic repression of TRPA1-dependent astrocyte reactivity confers neuroprotection in models of Lewy body dementia.
papers.summary: The paper shows that repeated ultra-low-intensity ultrasound (ULIUS) suppresses α-synuclein aggregation, astrocytic inflammation, neurodegeneration, and cognitive impairment in α-syn preformed-fibril models of Lewy body dementia. Mechanistically, ULIUS represses sustained astrocytic TRPA1-dependent calcium signaling and downstream TLR2 and pro-inflammatory cytokine expression.

papers.title: Advanced human iPSC-based preclinical model for Parkinson's disease with optogenetic alpha-synuclein aggregation.
papers.summary: The paper develops OASIS, an optogenetic system that rapidly induces α-synuclein aggregation and toxicity in Parkinson’s disease hiPSC-midbrain dopaminergic neurons and midbrain organoids. Screening identifies BAG956, which promotes autophagic clearance of pathological α-synuclein aggregates and reverses Parkinson’s disease phenotypes in cell and animal models.

papers.title: TNF-α-NF-κB activation through pathological α-Synuclein disrupts the BBB and exacerbates axonopathy.
papers.summary: The paper reports that α-synuclein aggregation activates the TNF-α-NF-κB pathway, increases brain endothelial permeability, disrupts the blood-brain barrier, and promotes axonal degeneration. The non-blood-brain-barrier-penetrating TNF-α inhibitor etanercept mitigated axonal degeneration in vivo.

papers.title: A candidate reference measurement procedure for the quantification of α-synuclein in cerebrospinal fluid using an SI traceable primary calibrator and multiple reaction monitoring.
papers.summary: The paper develops a candidate reference measurement procedure using an SI-traceable primary calibrator and targeted multiple reaction monitoring isotope dilution mass spectrometry to quantify α-synuclein in cerebrospinal fluid. The method accurately detected multiple proteotypic α-synuclein peptides in patient-derived CSF and may support standardized α-synuclein measurements in Parkinson’s disease and other synucleinopathies.

unread.title: Newborn screening for Krabbe disease in New York State: the first eight years' experience.
unread.why: This large-scale implementation study provides a validated newborn screening workflow with laboratory and clinical outcome data for infantile Krabbe disease.

unread.title: Intracranial calcification after cord blood neonatal transplantation for krabbe disease.
unread.why: The report provides direct three-year outcome data for cord-blood transplantation in a prenatally diagnosed newborn with Krabbe disease.

unread.title: Altered Trafficking and Processing of GALC Mutants Correlates with Globoid Cell Leukodystrophy Severity.
unread.why: The study shows that measuring GALC activity in lysosomal fractions and assessing trafficking better predicts disease severity than whole-cell lysate activity.

unread.title: Child Neurology: Krabbe disease: a potentially treatable white matter disorder.
unread.why: The title identifies hematopoietic stem cell transplantation as a potentially disease-modifying treatment for Krabbe disease, although the provided record contains no abstract or supporting data.

unread.title: Krabbe Disease
unread.why: This disease-specific review describes established diagnostic testing, newborn screening biomarkers, HSCT eligibility, and treatments for manifestations of Krabbe disease.

unread.title: Molecular characterization of mutations that cause globoid cell leukodystrophy and pharmacological rescue using small molecule chemical chaperones.
unread.why: The study directly demonstrates that alpha-lobeline rescues processing and increases activity of the D528N mutant GALC in cultured cells from the Krabbe disease mechanism.

unread.title: Infantile Krabbe disease (0-12 months), progression, and recommended endpoints for clinical trials.
unread.why: A prospective 137-patient study provides longitudinal HSCT outcomes, GALC and psychosine response data, survival measures, and clinically meaningful trial endpoints for infantile Krabbe disease.

unread.title: A mutation in the saposin A domain of the sphingolipid activator protein (prosaposin) gene results in a late-onset, chronic form of globoid cell leukodystrophy in the mouse.
unread.why: The engineered mouse develops a chronic globoid cell leukodystrophy phenotype and provides an in vivo model of saposin A-related galactosylceramide dysmetabolism relevant to Krabbe disease.

unread.title: Later onset phenotypes of Krabbe disease: results of the world-wide registry.
unread.why: The worldwide registry provides a cohort resource and longitudinal genotype, enzyme, phenotype, neurodiagnostic, and survival data for later-onset Krabbe disease.

unread.title: Mechanism-based combination treatment dramatically increases therapeutic efficacy in murine globoid cell leukodystrophy.
unread.why: In the murine Krabbe model, simultaneous gene therapy, substrate reduction, and bone marrow transplantation markedly extended lifespan and improved molecular and motor outcomes.

unread.title: Enzyme replacement therapy results in substantial improvements in early clinical phenotype in a mouse model of globoid cell leukodystrophy.
unread.why: Peripheral GALC injections in Twitcher mice improved motor performance, failure to thrive, brain GALC uptake, psychosine levels, and lifespan.

unread.title: Single-dose intracerebroventricular administration of galactocerebrosidase improves survival in a mouse model of globoid cell leukodystrophy.
unread.why: A single intracerebroventricular GALC dose reduced CNS psychosine and significantly extended survival in the mouse model of Krabbe disease.

unread.title: Early infantile Krabbe disease: results of the World-Wide Krabbe Registry.
unread.why: The registry reports disease-course, imaging, electrophysiological, biochemical, and survival data that can inform prognosis and trial design in early infantile Krabbe disease.

unread.title: Effects of treatments on inflammatory and apoptotic markers in the CNS of mice with globoid cell leukodystrophy.
unread.why: Anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective drugs reduced inflammatory or apoptotic markers and extended lifespan in GLD mice, although bone marrow transplantation produced the strongest effects.

unread.title: Krabbe disease: clinical, biochemical and molecular information on six new patients and successful retrospective diagnosis using stored newborn screening cards.
unread.why: This study validates galactocerebrosidase measurement from long-stored newborn-screening cards as a highly sensitive diagnostic test for Krabbe disease.

unread.title: Gene therapy for Krabbe disease: evidence from mouse and canine models.
unread.why: The review describes gene-therapy approaches tested in mouse and canine models that improve biochemical and pathological abnormalities and are ready for translational evaluation.

unread.title: Expression study of Krabbe Disease GALC missense variants – Insights from quantification profiles of residual enzyme activity, secretion and psychosine levels
unread.why: The study provides a human GALC-deficient oligodendrocyte model and functional assays linking GALC missense variants to enzyme activity, trafficking, psychosine levels, and clinical severity.

unread.title: Ceramide levels predict clinical severity in adult-onset Krabbe disease independent of extensive white matter hyperintensities.
unread.why: The study identifies plasma ceramide and sphingosine elevations as candidate severity biomarkers for adult-onset Krabbe disease when MRI burden does not reflect clinical severity.

unread.title: Genetic and Clinical Characteristics of Chinese Adult Patients With Krabbe Disease.
unread.why: The study combines sequencing with functional GALC assays to diagnose variants and strengthen genotype-phenotype interpretation in adult Krabbe disease.

unread.title: Krabbe disease: genetic aspects and progress toward therapy.
unread.why: Reports transplantation outcomes in Krabbe disease and experimental GALC restoration in twitcher oligodendrocytes using donor cells and viral vectors.

unread.title: Genetic ablation of acid ceramidase in Krabbe disease confirms the psychosine hypothesis and identifies a new therapeutic target.
unread.why: Shows that genetic or pharmacological suppression of acid ceramidase eliminates or reduces psychosine and markedly improves disease outcomes in the twitcher mouse model.

unread.title: Molecular Dynamics Simulations of 4 <i>GALC</i> Variants Causing Krabbe Disease.
unread.why: Applies lysosome-specific structural modeling and molecular dynamics to four pathogenic GALC variants to characterize flexibility, intramolecular interactions, and substrate-binding effects.

unread.title: Quantification profiles of enzyme activity, secretion, and psychosine levels of Krabbe disease galactosylceramidase missense variants.
unread.why: Builds a disease-specific cellular platform that quantifies GALC activity, secretion, trafficking, and psychosine for variant prognosis, chaperone target selection, and drug discovery.

unread.title: The Twitcher mouse: an enzymatically authentic model of human globoid cell leukodystrophy (Krabbe disease).
unread.why: Establishes the twitcher mouse as a clinically, histologically, and enzymatically faithful in vivo model of human Krabbe disease.

unread.title: Cloning and expression of cDNA encoding human galactocerebrosidase, the enzyme deficient in globoid cell leukodystrophy.
unread.why: Provides and validates a human GALC cDNA expression resource that increased GALC activity sixfold and supports functional, diagnostic, and treatment studies.

unread.title: Insights into Krabbe disease from structures of galactocerebrosidase.
unread.why: Defines atomic structures of GALC and its substrate complex, enabling mechanistic analysis of pathogenic mutations and structure-guided identification of pharmacological chaperones.

unread.title: Long-term neurodevelopmental outcomes of hematopoietic stem cell transplantation for late-infantile Krabbe disease.
unread.why: A prospective longitudinal study shows that HSCT prolongs survival and improves cognitive, language, and motor outcomes in late-infantile Krabbe disease, especially when performed presymptomatically.

unread.title: MR imaging and proton MR spectroscopy in adult Krabbe disease.
unread.why: The study identifies characteristic MRI and spectroscopic findings that can support recognition and phenotypic characterization of adult Krabbe disease.

unread.title: Two different mutations are responsible for Krabbe disease in the Druze and Moslem Arab populations in Israel.
unread.why: The authors validated a simple PCR-restriction assay for detecting two prevalent GALC alleles and enabling accurate carrier testing in Israeli Druze and Moslem Arab populations.

unread.title: Direct microglia replacement reveals pathologic and therapeutic contributions of brain macrophages to a monogenic neurological disease.
unread.why: In the Galc-deficient twitcher mouse, direct replacement of more than 80% of microglia normalized disease-associated transcriptional changes, rescued histopathology, and doubled average survival.

unread.title: Genetic ablation of Saposin-D in Krabbe disease eliminates psychosine accumulation but does not significantly improve demyelination.
unread.why: The engineered twitcher mouse specifically ablates psychosine accumulation and provides causal evidence that persistent demyelination can involve psychosine-independent, Saposin-D-dependent inflammatory mechanisms.

unread.title: Investigating the Cellular Effects of GALC Dosing in Enzyme Replacement Therapy for Krabbe Disease Supports the Role of Nanomedicine.
unread.why: The study produces active recombinant GALC, demonstrates dose-dependent rescue of GALC-deficient primary cells, and develops a polymeric nanovector strategy for ERT with dose-dependent autophagy and viability effects.

unread.title: Amelioration of Inflammation and Metabolic Blockage in GALC Deficient Mice After Enzyme Replacement Therapy via Extracellular Vesicles.
unread.why: A single intrathecal dose of GALC-loaded extracellular vesicles reduced cortical psychosine, astrogliosis, and microgliosis in neonatal GALC-deficient mice, although it did not extend survival.

unread.title: Durable Global Correction of CNS and PNS and Lifespan Rescue in Murine Globoid Cell Leukodystrophy via AAV9-Mediated Monotherapy.
unread.why: A single intracranial AAV9-GALC treatment produced durable GALC and psychosine correction, preserved myelin and motor function, and nearly normalized lifespan in a murine GLD model.

unread.title: Abnormal Splicing of <i>GALC</i> Transcripts Underlies Unusual Cases of Krabbe Disease.
unread.why: The study demonstrates an integrated diagnostic workflow that functionally classifies novel deep-intronic and splice-site GALC variants in Krabbe disease.

unread.title: Long-term neurological outcome after hematopoietic stem cell transplant in juvenile Krabbe disease.
unread.why: Long-term patient data support HSCT for juvenile Krabbe disease and identify standardized pre-transplant measures associated with neurological outcome.

unread.title: Progressive accumulation of toxic metabolite in a genetic leukodystrophy.
unread.why: The paper directly demonstrates progressive psychosine accumulation in Krabbe disease and its mechanistic relevance across mouse, dog, and human disease tissue.

unread.title: Identification of hematopoietic stem cell-specific miRNAs enables gene therapy of globoid cell leukodystrophy.
unread.why: HSC-restricted GALC expression using miR-126 target sequences avoided progenitor toxicity and successfully treated a mouse model of GLD.

unread.title: AAV-mediated expression of galactocerebrosidase in brain results in attenuated symptoms and extended life span in murine models of globoid cell leukodystrophy.
unread.why: Direct brain delivery of AAV1-GALC improved myelination, pathology, symptoms, and lifespan in neonatal murine GLD, although survival was not normalized.

unread.title: Clinical outcomes of children with abnormal newborn screening results for Krabbe disease in New York State.
unread.why: The New York screening program provides operational data on population screening, confirmatory neurodiagnostic assessment, and early HSCT decision-making for Krabbe disease.

unread.title: The long-term outcomes of presymptomatic infants transplanted for Krabbe disease: report of the workshop held on July 11 and 12, 2008, Holiday Valley, New York.
unread.why: This workshop consolidates clinical and animal evidence on HCT and establishes a framework for evaluating long-term neurological deterioration in presymptomatic Krabbe patients.

unread.title: Late-onset Krabbe disease (globoid cell leukodystrophy): clinical and biochemical features of 15 cases.
unread.why: The 15-case series defines recognizable late-onset clinical and biochemical phenotypes and reports initial clinical outcomes of bone marrow transplantation.

unread.title: Combined hematopoietic and lentiviral gene-transfer therapies in newborn Twitcher mice reveal contemporaneous neurodegeneration and demyelination in Krabbe disease.
unread.why: Combined hematopoietic and lentiviral GALC delivery in newborn Twitcher mice improved GALC activity, myelin preservation, locomotion, and survival while exposing residual neuronal degeneration.

unread.title: Macrophages Expressing GALC Improve Peripheral Krabbe Disease by a Mechanism Independent of Cross-Correction.
unread.why: The novel cellular model shows that healthy GALC-expressing macrophages can reduce globoid cells through myelin clearance independent of conventional enzyme cross-correction, explaining part of HSCT benefit.

unread.title: Late-onset Krabbe disease is predominant in Japan and its mutant precursor protein undergoes more effective processing than the infantile-onset form.
unread.why: Functional enzyme testing and structural modeling establish a reusable framework for relating GALC variants to activity, protein processing, and infantile versus late-onset disease severity.

unread.title: Diffusion tensor imaging detects abnormalities in the corticospinal tracts of neonates with infantile Krabbe disease.
unread.why: DTI with tractography objectively detected corticospinal-tract abnormalities in asymptomatic neonatal Krabbe disease and was proposed as a progression marker.

unread.title: Enzyme replacement therapy of a novel humanized mouse model of globoid cell leukodystrophy.
unread.why: The authors generated a humanized Krabbe disease mouse model and tested intravenous rhGALC, demonstrating tissue delivery and partial psychosine reduction but no rescue of major neuropathology or lifespan.

unread.title: Expression of individual mutations and haplotypes in the galactocerebrosidase gene identified by the newborn screening program in New York State and in confirmed cases of Krabbe's disease.
unread.why: Functional expression testing of 140 GALC constructs showed that some variants and haplotypes reduce enzyme activity, providing a concrete assay for interpreting screen-positive newborns.

unread.title: Quantitative analysis of diffusion tensor imaging data in serial assessment of Krabbe disease.
unread.why: Serial DTI anisotropy measurements distinguished early from late transplantation groups and correlated with neurodevelopmental outcomes in Krabbe disease.

unread.title: Prevalent mutations in the GALC gene of patients with Krabbe disease of Dutch and other European origin.
unread.why: The study identified recurrent GALC variants in European Krabbe disease cohorts and demonstrated their practical use for carrier and prenatal diagnosis.

unread.title: Oxidative stress as a therapeutic target in globoid cell leukodystrophy.
unread.why: N-acetylcysteine reduced oxidized proteins and improved disease-marker histology in twitcher mice but produced no clinical improvement, even when combined with bone marrow transplantation.

unread.title: Stem cell transplantation for adult-onset krabbe disease: report of a case.
unread.why: A symptomatic adult-onset Krabbe disease patient achieved sustained peripheral GALC normalization, symptom stabilization, and gait and balance improvement for 24 months after HSCT.

unread.title: A novel brain-penetrant oral UGT8 inhibitor decreases in vivo galactosphingolipid biosynthesis in murine Krabbe disease.
unread.why: RA 5557 is directly tested in a Galc-deficient Krabbe mouse model and reduces psychosine, galactosylceramide, and inflammatory markers in vivo.

unread.title: Evidence and Recommendation for Infantile Krabbe Disease Newborn Screening.
unread.why: This article describes a clinically actionable newborn-screening and psychosine-stratification pathway for early diagnosis and urgent HSCT in infantile Krabbe disease.

unread.title: CD8+ T cell depletion prevents neuropathology in a mouse model of globoid cell leukodystrophy.
unread.why: CD8+ T-cell depletion directly prevents neuropathology, demyelination, morbidity, and mortality in a mouse model of Krabbe disease.

unread.title: Adult Krabbe Disease That Was Successfully Treated with Intravenous Immunoglobulin.
unread.why: In a patient with adult Krabbe disease presenting inflammatory demyelinating neuropathy-like symptoms, IVIg produced symptom improvement and may be a transferable treatment in selected cases.

unread.title: Low Psychosine in Krabbe Disease with Onset in Late Infancy: A Case Report.
unread.why: The case provides direct evidence that psychosine is an important but imperfect risk-stratification biomarker and supports integrated interpretation with genotype, enzyme activity, and clinical findings.

unread.title: Favorable outcome of hematopoietic stem cell transplantation in late-onset Krabbe disease.
unread.why: The report provides direct evidence of normalized GALC activity, reduced CNS lesions, and functional improvement after HSCT in late-onset Krabbe disease.

unread.title: Compound heterozygous pathogenic variants in the GALC gene cause infant-onset Krabbe disease.
unread.why: The study experimentally validates genetic and molecular testing approaches for diagnosing infantile Krabbe disease.

unread.title: Cell-based high-throughput screening identifies galactocerebrosidase enhancers as potential small-molecule therapies for Krabbe's disease.
unread.why: The paper identifies three tested small-molecule GALC enhancers and provides a disease-relevant high-throughput screening platform with experimental activity and stabilization data.

unread.title: Chimeric enzymes enhance treatment potential for globoid cell leukodystrophy through hematopoietic stem cell gene therapy.
unread.why: The study demonstrates a chimeric-enzyme HSPC gene-therapy strategy that improves GALC production, secretion, delivery, and neural cross-correction in globoid cell leukodystrophy models.

unread.title: Clinical and molecular findings in 6 Turkish cases with Krabbe disease.
unread.why: The study provides a molecular diagnostic workflow and a case series documenting GALC variants and large deletions relevant to Krabbe screening and genetic counseling.

unread.title: Weighing the evidence for newborn screening for early-infantile Krabbe disease.
unread.why: The systematic review evaluates an existing newborn-screening and treatment pathway with evidence from screened newborns and transplanted children.

unread.title: Chaperone therapy for Krabbe disease: potential for late-onset GALC mutations.
unread.why: The study experimentally tests NOEV as a GALC chaperone and shows enhanced activity and maturation for several late-onset Krabbe mutations in patient fibroblasts.

unread.title: Transgenic rescue of Krabbe disease in the twitcher mouse.
unread.why: The study demonstrates durable rescue of GALC deficiency, neurological pathology, and motor dysfunction by introducing a human GALC transgene into the twitcher mouse.

unread.title: Metabolomic, lipidomic, and N-glycomic analyses of a human cell model of Krabbe disease reveal treatable deficits in glycosylation and serine-ceramide metabolism
unread.why: The study directly identifies pharmacological normalization of psychosine by tezacaftor and a glycosylation defect that supports galactose supplementation in a human Krabbe disease model.

unread.title: Laboratory-Positive Findings for Six Lysosomal Storage Disorders in Pediatric Dried Blood Spot Samples from Uzbekistan: A 2025 Retrospective Descriptive Study
unread.why: The report evaluates a multiplex dried-blood-spot enzyme screening assay and provides Krabbe disease screening data from 105 laboratory-positive pediatric samples.

unread.title: Unveiling Key Immune Genes and Drug Candidates for Krabbe Disease in Human iPSCs-derived NSCs
unread.why: The study provides a disease-specific iPSC-derived neural stem-cell model and computational screening data for four repurposed or proposed drug candidates.

unread.title: [From gene to disease; Krabbe disease and galactosylceramidase deficiency].
unread.why: The paper identifies established enzyme and molecular testing approaches that permit timely diagnosis and prenatal diagnosis of Krabbe disease.

unread.title: Homozygosity for a Clinically Significant <i>GALC</i> Haplotype Associated with Late-Infantile Krabbe Disease Detected on Newborn Screening: Implications for Clinical Management and Genetic Counseling.
unread.why: The case provides a practical framework integrating newborn-screen GALC activity, psychosine levels, genotype interpretation, and longitudinal neuroimaging for clinical management.

unread.title: Perinatal loss of galactosylceramidase in both oligodendrocytes and microglia is crucial for the pathogenesis of Krabbe disease in mice.
unread.why: The authors developed cell-specific Galc knockout and coculture models that dissect how oligodendrocyte and microglial GALC loss contributes to Krabbe disease pathogenesis.

unread.title: The analysis of genetic aberrations in children with inherited neurometabolic and neurodevelopmental disorders.
unread.why: The report confirms Krabbe disease by identifying biallelic GALC variants while excluding PSAP-related disease, supporting an integrated genetic diagnostic workflow.

unread.title: Chronic Rapamycin administration via drinking water mitigates the pathological phenotype in a Krabbe disease mouse model through autophagy activation.
unread.why: Chronic rapamycin in the Twitcher mouse improved selected motor outcomes, reduced astrogliosis and p62 aggregates, and partially lowered spinal-cord psychosine.

unread.title: Brain accumulation of lactosylceramide characterizes GALC deficiency in a zebrafish model of Krabbe disease.
unread.why: The study develops and validates GALC-deficient zebrafish models that reproduce Krabbe disease phenotypes and identifies brain lactosylceramide accumulation as a measurable mechanistic biomarker.

unread.title: High Prevalence of GALC Gene Variants in Adults With Neurodegenerative Conditions.
unread.why: The study demonstrates the use of GALC sequencing and activity measurements to identify pathogenic variants, reduced enzyme function, and late-onset Krabbe disease among adults with neurodegenerative symptoms.

unread.title: Ablation of lipocalin-2 reduces neuroinflammation in a mouse model of Krabbe disease.
unread.why: Genetic ablation of Lcn2 in GALC-deficient mice substantially reduces neuroinflammation and modestly improves survival and disease progression, providing a testable therapeutic target.

unread.title: The Effect of Donepezil Hydrochloride in the Twitcher Mouse Model of Krabbe Disease.
unread.why: Donepezil treatment in the twitcher mouse model preserves myelin, reduces glial reactivity, improves behavior, and increases lifespan, supporting its repurposing for Krabbe disease.

unread.title: Two-tiered newborn screening for infantile Krabbe disease allows timely treatment initiation and avoids false-positive results.
unread.why: The study validates psychosine as a second-tier newborn-screening test that shortens diagnosis time, reduces false positives, and supports timely hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation.

unread.title: Peripheral Neuropathy as an Early Marker in Newborn-Screened Krabbe Disease: The Value of Pre-Confirmatory Neurophysiological Testing.
unread.why: Electrodiagnostic testing detected severe mixed sensorimotor polyneuropathy in two screen-positive infants and provided an actionable early severity measure before molecular confirmation or transplantation.

unread.title: Neuronal inclusions of α-synuclein contribute to the pathogenesis of Krabbe disease.
unread.why: The study directly examines human Krabbe brains and the twitcher mouse while demonstrating psychosine-driven α-synuclein fibrillization, providing disease-specific mechanistic assays and a relevant animal model.
